en: The act of preventing or hindering; obstruction of action, access, or approach; thwarting.
Any measure intended to limit health-related risks (such as information campaigns, vaccination, early diagnosis etc.).

prevention.ety: From Middle English prevencion, from Medieval Latin prēventiō.

ex.en: September 10 is World Suicide Prevention Day.
ex.ja: 9月10日は世界自殺予防デーです。

ex.en: This is Fire Prevention Week.
ex.ja: 今週は火災予防週間です。

ex.en: This museum is equipped with a fire prevention system.
ex.ja: この美術館には防火の設備がある。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ vent（来る）+ ion。先回りすること →「予防・防止」。

en: A device for moving or compressing a liquid or gas.
An instance of the action of a pump; one stroke of a pump; any action similar to pumping.
To use a pump; to move (water or other liquid) by means of a pump.
To inject or pour (something) into someone or something in a manner similar to a pump.

pump.ety:
From Middle English pumpe, possibly from Middle Dutch pompe (“pipe, water conduit”) or Middle Low German pumpe (“pump”), probably ultimately imitative.
Compare Dutch pompen, German pumpen, and Danish pompe; also Spanish bomba (“pump”).

ex.ja: ポンプはちゃんと動かなかった。

ex.en: The function of the heart is to pump blood.
ex.ja: 心臓の働きは血液を送り出す事である。

ex.en: The human heart is analogous to a pump.
ex.ja: 心臓とポンプは似かよっている。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 pompe から。擬音的な語とされる。「ポンプ・くみ出す」。

en: Any form of personal, retaliatory action against an individual, institution, or group for some alleged or perceived harm or injustice.
A win by a previous loser.
To take revenge for (a particular harmful action) or on behalf of (its victim); to avenge.
To take one's revenge (on or upon someone).

revenge.ety: From Middle French revenge, a derivation from revenger, from Old French revengier (possibly influenced by Old Occitan revènge (“revenge, comeback”), from Old Occitan revenir (“to come back”)), a variant of Middle French revancher (whence deverbal French revanche), from Old French revenchier. The variants Old French vengier (whence French venger) and Old French venchier are both descended from Latin vindicō, with stress-conditioned different parallel development in the inflectional forms. Doublet of revanche. Compare avenge and vengeance.

ex.en: I got a little revenge on him.
ex.ja: ちょっと仕返ししてやった。

ex.en: The officer seemed to be afraid of their revenge.
ex.ja: その将校は彼らの復讐を恐れているようだった。

ex.en: I will take my revenge on him.
ex.ja: 私は彼に報復するつもりだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 revengier ＝ re + vengier（仕返しする）。ラテン語 vindicare。vengeance、vindicate と同じ。

en: To be enough (for)
To meet the needs of, to fulfill the wishes or requirements of (someone).

ex.ja: あなたは自分の人生に満足していますね？

ex.ja: 結果にちっとも満足しなかった。

ex.en: I am not satisfied with my performance today.
ex.ja: 今日の演奏の出来は私の意にかなったものではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 satisfacere ＝ satis（十分に）+ facere（する）。「十分にする」→「満足させる」。asset と同じ satis。

To err.
An act or instance of slipping.
A woman's undergarment worn under a skirt or dress to conceal unwanted nudity that may otherwise be revealed by the skirt or dress itself…

en: Being more than what is necessary, or what must be used or reserved; not wanted, or not used; superfluous.
Held in reserve, to be used in an emergency.
The act of sparing; moderation; restraint.
Parsimony; frugal use.
To desist; to stop; to refrain.
To refrain from inflicting harm; to use mercy or forbearance.

spare.ety:
From Middle English spare, spar, from Old English spær (“sparing, scant”), from Proto-Germanic *sparaz, from Proto-Indo-European *sph₁rós, from the root *speh₁-.
Compare Dutch spaar(zaam), German spar(sam) and spär(lich), Swedish spar(sam), Icelandic sparr (“sparing”); also Latin (pro)sperus (“lucky”), Old Church Slavonic споръ (sporŭ, “plentiful”), Albanian shperr (“earn money”), Persian سپار (sepâr, “entrust; deposit”), Ancient Greek σπαρνός (sparnós, “rare”), Sanskrit स्फिर (sphirá, “thick”).

ex.en: I spend what time I can spare reading.
ex.ja: 出来る限りの時間は読書に費やす。

ex.en: I cannot buy spare parts for this car.
ex.ja: この車の予備の部品を買うことができない。

ex.en: Do you have a few minutes to spare?
ex.ja: お時間を少しいただいてもよろしいでしょうか。

note.ja: 古英語 sparian（惜しむ・節約する）から。「節約してとっておく」→「予備の・割く」。

en: Specialised, involving detailed knowledge of a restricted topic.
Someone who is an expert in, or devoted to, some specific branch of study or research.
A player on a team who primarily employs one particular skill or takes one particular role.

specialist.ety: Borrowed from French spécialiste, equivalent to special + -ist.

en: A person whom one does not know; a person who is neither a friend nor an acquaintance.
An outsider or foreigner.

stranger.ety: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

ex.ja: どうして見ず知らずの男が自分の名前を知っているんだろう？

ex.en: I saw a stranger steal into his house.
ex.ja: 私は見知らぬ人が彼の家に忍び込むのを見た。

ex.en: I saw a stranger standing at the door.
ex.ja: 私は見知らぬ人が戸口に立っているのを見た。

note.ja: strange（見知らぬ）+ -er。「見知らぬ人」。

To furnish (a container, etc.) with a tap (noun etymology 1, noun sense 2.2) so that liquid can be drawn.

en: Capable, worthy, or sure of being accepted or received with pleasure; welcome; gratifying; pleasing to a receiver.
Barely worthy, less than excellent; passable.
Someone or something that is acceptable.

acceptable.ety:

ex.ja: 彼の仕事はまずまずの出来だが、とても優秀とは言えなかった。

The first stage of a deal, in which players bid to determine the final contract.
To sell at an auction.

auction.ety: From Latin auctiō (“an increase, auction”), from augere (“to increase”).

ex.ja: 競売でその絵画を手に入れた。

ex.en: Tom bought this horse at an auction.

ex.ja: 競売でその絵画を手に入れた。

en: The unordered state of matter in classical accounts of cosmogony.
Any state of disorder; a confused or amorphous mixture or conglomeration.

Etymology tree

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek χάος (kháos, “vast chasm, void”). Doublet of gas, which was borrowed through Dutch. Displaced native Old English dwolma.
In Early Modern English, used in the sense of the original Greek word. In the meaning “primordial matter” from the 16th century. Figurative usage in the sense “confusion, disorder” from the 17th century. The technical sense in mathematics and science dates from the 1960s.

ex.en: The accident caused traffic chaos.
ex.ja: その事故で交通は大混乱に陥った。

ex.en: I expect every day is chaos for families with small children.
ex.ja: 小さな子供のいる家庭は、毎日がどたばたして大変だと思う。

ex.en: The entire theater turned to chaos when somebody cried "Fire!".
ex.ja: 誰かが「火事だ」と叫んだら、劇場全体が大混乱になった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 khaos（大きな裂け目・虚空）から。天地創造前の混沌 →「大混乱」。gas はこの語から作られた。

en: To make something by merging parts.
To make up the whole; to constitute.

compose.ety: From Middle English composen, from Old French composer (“to compose, compound, adjust, settle”), from com- + poser, as an adaptation of Latin componere (“to put together, compose”), from com- (“together”) + ponere (“to put, place”).

ex.en: The committee is composed of teachers and parents.
ex.ja: 委員会は教師と親から成り立っている。

ex.en: The committee was composed entirely of young teachers.
ex.ja: その委員会は全員若い先生で構成されていた。

ex.en: Please compose a draft of the proposal idea.
ex.ja: 提案書をまとめて下さい。

en: The act, process or ability of concentrating; the process of becoming concentrated, or the state of being concentrated.
The direction of attention to a specific object.

ex.en: I immediately lost my concentration.
ex.ja: すぐに集中力を無くしてしまった。

ex.en: It's the sort of work that calls for a high level of concentration.
ex.ja: それは高レベルの集中力を必要とする種類の仕事だ。

Made of copper (etymology 1, noun sense 1).
Having the reddish-brown colour of copper.
To coat or sheathe (something) with copper (etymology 1, noun sense 1).

ex.en: The atomic number of copper is 29.

An organized group of people united by a common purpose.

corps.ety: From French corps d'armée (literally “army body”), from Latin corpus (“body”). Doublet of corpse and corpus. See also English riff.

ex.ja: 平和部隊にいる頃に彼女は教職の第一歩を踏み出した。

en: To begin to brighten with daylight.
To start to appear or become obvious.
The morning twilight period immediately before sunrise.
The rising of the sun.

dawn.ety: From Middle English dawnen, either a back-formation from dawnynge or a modification of dawen (“to dawn”) after it. The noun is from the verb.

ex.en: Finally dawn broke; the long night had ended.
ex.ja: ようやく夜が明けて長い夜が終わった。

ex.en: I wake up every morning before the dawn.
ex.ja: 毎朝、夜明け前に目が覚めます。

ex.en: The meaning dawned upon me at last.
ex.ja: やっとその意味が分かった。

From Middle English disputen, from Old French desputer (French disputer), from Latin disputāre (“to dispute, discuss, examine, compute, estimate”), from dis- (“apart”) + putāre

ex.en: We disputed for hours about what to write.
ex.ja: 何を書くべきか私たちは何時間も論争した。

ex.en: He refused to get involved in the dispute.
ex.ja: 彼はそのもめごとに関わり合いを持つ事を拒んだ。

ex.en: That dispute has been settled once and for all.
ex.ja: その論争は完全に片が付いた。

note.ja: ラテン語 disputare ＝ dis（ばらばらに）+ putare（考える）。「考えを分けて論じる」→「論争」。compute と同じ put。

en: To kill, especially as punishment for a capital crime.
To carry out; to put into effect.

execute.ety: From Old French executer (French exécuter), from Latin exsecutus, past participle of exsequor (“to follow (up/through)”, particularly in the sense “to go through with a deed or punishment”), from ex- (“out”) + sequor (“to follow”).

ex.en: He asked his brother to execute his will.
ex.ja: 彼は弟に遺言を実行してくれと頼んだ。

ex.en: There are times when innocent people get executed.
ex.ja: 無罪の人々が処刑されている場合もある。

ex.en: It is difficult to execute the task.
ex.ja: その仕事を実行するのは困難だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 exsequi ＝ ex + sequi（追う）。「最後まで追う」→「実行する」→ 刑を「執行する・処刑する」。

en: Done or occurring often; common.
Occurring at short intervals.
To visit often.

frequent.ety: From Old French frequent, from Latin frequens (“crowded, crammed, frequent, repeated, etc.”), possibly from a Proto-Indo-European *bʰrekʷ- (“to cram together”).

ex.en: I came into frequent contact with foreign students.
ex.ja: 私は外国の学生としばしば接触した。

ex.en: My boss called me down for frequent absence from work.
ex.ja: 上司はよく欠勤するといって私を叱った。

ex.en: He makes frequent visits to Japan on business.
ex.ja: 彼は商用でしばしば日本にやってくる。

note.ja: ラテン語 frequens（ぎっしり詰まった・頻繁な）から。「頻繁な」→（場所に）「よく通う」。

en: To collect normally separate things.
Especially, to harvest food.
A plait or fold in cloth, made by drawing a thread through it; a pucker.
The inclination forward of the axle journals to keep the wheels from working outward.

gather.ety: From Middle English gaderen, from Old English gaderian (“to gather, assemble”), from Proto-West Germanic *gadurōn (“to bring together, unite, gather”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰedʰ- (“to unite, assemble, keep”).

ex.en: A lot of children gathered in the garden.
ex.ja: たくさんの子供が庭に集まった。

ex.en: A variety of people gathered at the meeting.
ex.ja: その会合に集まった人たちは多種多様だった。

ex.en: The American Ambassador was invited to the gathering.
ex.ja: アメリカ大使がその集まりに招待された。

note.ja: 古英語 gaderian から。together と同じ語根。「集める」→ 情報を集めて「推測する」。

en: Very funny; causing great merriment and laughter.
Full of hilarity; merry.

hilarious.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin hilaris (“cheerful”) + -ious, from Ancient Greek ἱλαρός (hilarós, “cheerful, merry”).

ex.en: The movie was so hilarious that we laughed the whole time.
ex.ja: その映画はとても面白くて、私たちはずっと笑っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 hilaris（陽気な）から。ギリシャ語 hilaros。「大笑いさせる」。exhilarate と同じ。

en: The edge of the paper, typically left blank when printing but sometimes used for annotations etc.
The edge or border of any flat surface.
To add a margin to; to furnish with a margin.
To enter (notes etc.) into the margin.

margin.ety: From Middle English margyn, from Latin marginem (possibly via Old French margin), accusative of margō (“edge, brink, border, margin”). Doublet of marge and margo.

ex.en: This product brought us a large margin.
ex.ja: この製品のお陰で我が社は大きな利益をあげた。

ex.en: I allowed a margin of ten minutes.
ex.ja: 私は１０分の余裕を見ておいた。

ex.en: We left a margin for error in our estimates.
ex.ja: 我々は誤差を見込んで余裕をとっておいた。

note.ja: ラテン語 margo（縁）から。「縁・余白」→ 差の「幅」→「利ざや」。marginal。

en: To spoil; to ruin; to scathe; to damage.
A blemish.

mar.ety: Inherited from Middle English merren, from Old English mierran (“to mar, disturb, confuse; scatter, squander, waste; upset, hinder, obstruct; err”), from Proto-Germanic *marzijaną (“to disturb, hinder”), from Proto-Indo-European *mers- (“to annoy, disturb, neglect, forget, ignore”). Cognate with Scots mer, mar (“to obstruct, impede, spoil, ruin”), Dutch marren (“to push along, delay, hinder”), dialectal German merren (“to entangle”), Icelandic merja (“to bruise, crush”), Gothic 𐌼𐌰𐍂𐌶𐌾𐌰𐌽 (marzjan, “to annoy, bother, disturb, offend”), Lithuanian miršti (“to forget, lose, become oblivious, die”),

ex.en: There is no sign of life on Mars.
ex.ja: 火星には生物の形跡はない。

ex.en: I think I want to go to Mars.
ex.ja: 火星へ行ってみたいと思う。

ex.en: It won't be long before we can travel to Mars.
ex.ja: 火星へ旅行できる日も遠くはあるまい。

note.ja: 古英語 merran（妨げる）から。「損なう・台無しにする」。

en: Any mechanical means for the conversion or control of motion, or the transmission or control of power.
Any combination of cams, gears, links, belts, chains and logical mechanical elements.

mechanism.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *megʰ-der.?
Ancient Greek μηχᾰνή (mēkhănḗ)der.
New Latin mechanismuslbor.
English mechanism
Learned borrowing from New Latin mechanismus.

ex.en: The mechanism of this machine is complicated.
ex.ja: この機械のメカニズムは複雑です。

ex.en: Economics is the study of economic mechanisms.
ex.ja: 経済学は経済の仕組みを研究する学問である。

ex.en: Its mechanism will cease to work.
ex.ja: その機能は働かなくなるだろう。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 mēkhanē（機械・装置）から。「仕組み」。machine、mechanic と同じ。

en: Not excessive; acting in moderation.
More than mild but less than severe.
One who holds an intermediate position between extremes, as in politics.
One of a party in Scottish Church history dominant in the 18th century, lax in doctrine and discipline, but intolerant of evangelicalism …
To reduce the excessiveness of (something).
To become less excessive.

moderate.ety: From Middle English moderat(e) (“moderate, temperate”), borrowed from Latin moderātus, perfect active participle of moderor (“to regulate, to restrain, to moderate”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from moder-, modes-, a stem appearing also in modestus (“moderate, discreet, modest”), from modus (“a measure”); see mode and modest. Doublet of moderato. Displaced native Old English ġemetlīċ (“moderate”) and metegian (“to moderate”). Cognate with French modéré.

ex.en: The weather in Florida is generally moderate.
ex.ja: 概してフロリダの気候は穏やかだ。

ex.en: Good health consists of proper eating and moderate exercise.
ex.ja: 健康は適切な食事と適度な運動にある。

ex.en: I always drive at a moderate speed.
ex.ja: 私はいつも適度なスピードで運転しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 moderare（ほどよくする）から。modus（尺度）。「適度な」→「司会をする」。mode、modest と同じ mod。

en: A theatrical work, combining drama, music, song and sometimes dance; usually, one sung-through, based on classical music and seen as more…
The score for such a work.

opera.ety: Borrowed from Italian opera. Doublet of oeuvre, opus, and ure.

ex.en: This is an opera in five acts.
ex.ja: この歌劇は５幕ものです。

ex.en: We are watching a class at the Paris Opera.
ex.ja: 私たちはパリ・オペラ座の踊りのレッスンを見ています。

ex.en: He wrote the score of the opera.
ex.ja: 彼はオペラを書いた。

note.ja: ラテン語 opus（仕事・作品）の複数形 opera から。作品の集まり →「オペラ・歌劇」。operation と同じ oper。

en: To surmount (a physical or abstract obstacle); to prevail over, to get the better of.
To prevail.
The burden or recurring theme in a song.
A surplus.
That has been overcome, prevailed over.

overcome.ety: Inherited from Middle English overcomen, inherited from Old English ofercuman (“to overcome, subdue, compel, conquer, obtain, attain, reach, overtake”). By surface analysis, over- + come. Cognate with Dutch overkomen, German überkommen, Danish overkomme, Swedish överkomma.

ex.en: He did his best to overcome his enemy.
ex.ja: 彼は敵を打ち負かすのに全力を尽くした。

ex.en: I must pull myself together to overcome this incident.
ex.ja: わたしはこの出来事を乗り越えるためにしっかりしなければならない。

ex.en: We helped each other to overcome the difficulties.
ex.ja: 我々は力を合わせて困難を克服した。

note.ja: over（越えて）+ come（来る）。「乗り越えてくる」→「克服する」。

en: Equally distant from one another at all points.
Having the same overall direction; the comparison is indicated with "to".
With a parallel relationship.
One of a set of parallel lines.
Direction conformable to that of another line.
To construct or place something parallel to something else.
Of a path etc: To be parallel to something else.

parallel.ety: From Middle French parallèle and its etymon Latin parallēlus, parallēlos. The verb is from the noun. See also para- and allo-.

ex.en: The river runs parallel to the main street.
ex.ja: その川はメインストリートと平行に流れている。

ex.en: The two streets run parallel to one another.
ex.ja: ２本の道路は平行に走っている。

ex.en: The two streets run parallel to each other.
ex.ja: ２本の道路は平行に走っている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 parallēlos ＝ para（そばに）+ allēlōn（互いに）。「互いにそばにある」→「平行の・類似した」。

en: A paragraph or section of text or music with particular meaning.
Part of a path or journey.
To pass something, such as a pathogen or stem cell, through a host or medium.
Of a bird: Less than a year old but living on its own, having left the nest.

passage.ety: Borrowed into Middle English from Old French passage, from passer (“to pass”).

ex.en: We found a secret passage into the building.
ex.ja: 我々はその建物への秘密の通路を発見した。

ex.en: This world is but a place of passage.
ex.ja: この世は仮の宿に過ぎない。

ex.en: There is no passage for big vehicles here.
ex.ja: ここは大型車の通行は禁止されている。

note.ja: pass（通る）+ age。通り抜けること・通り道 →「通路・通過・（文章の）一節」。

en: A hole in the ground.
An area at a racetrack used for refueling and repairing the vehicles during a race.
To make pits in; to mark with little hollows.
To put (an animal) into a pit for fighting.

pit.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-West Germanic *puti
Old English pytt
Middle English pit
English pit
From Middle English pit, pet, püt, from Old English pytt, from Proto-West Germanic *puti, from Latin puteus (“trench, pit, well”), although there are phonetic difficulties.

ex.en: Not many people actually fall into the pit.
ex.ja: 実際に落とし穴に落ちる人なんてそうそういない。

ex.en: He fell into the bottomless pit.
ex.ja: 彼は奈落の底に落ちた。

ex.en: Naomi fell in the orchestra pit during her performance and broke her arm.
ex.ja: 直美は公演中にオケピに落ちて腕を折った。

note.ja: 「穴」は古英語 pytt から。ラテン語 puteus（井戸）。「果物の種」はオランダ語 pit（芯）からで別語。

en: Of or pertaining to psychology.
Relating to the mind and behavior or to the mental, emotional, and behavioral characteristics pertaining to a specified person, group, or…

ex.ja: 彼の記憶喪失は物理的な記憶障害というよりは心理的な障害である。

ex.en: Furries face psychological hurdles in learning Spanish.
ex.ja: ケモナーはスペイン語を学ぶ心理的ハードルが高い。

note.ja: psychology + -ical。ギリシャ語 psykhē（魂・心）+ logia。「心理的な」。

en: A journey or effort in pursuit of a goal (often lengthy, ambitious, or fervent); a mission.
A task that a player may complete in order to gain a reward or advance the story.
To seek or pursue a goal; to undertake a mission or job.
To search for something; to seek.

quest.ety: From Middle English quest, queste; partly from Anglo-Norman queste, Old French queste (“acquisition, search, hunt”), and partly from their source, Latin quaesta (“tribute, tax, inquiry, search”), noun use of quaesita, the feminine past participle of quaerō (“to ask, seek”). Doublet of question.

ex.en: And just like that, the quest began.
ex.ja: いきなりクエストが始まった。

ex.en: They explored the desert in quest of buried treasure.
ex.ja: 彼らは埋蔵された宝物を求めて砂漠を探検した。

ex.en: Gulliver traveled in quest of adventure.
ex.ja: ガリバーは冒険を求めて旅をした。

note.ja: ラテン語 quaerere（求める）から。求めること →「探求・追求」。question（質問）、request（依頼）も同じ。

en: The shooting forth of anything from a point or surface, like diverging rays of light.
The process of radiating waves or particles.

radiation.ety: Borrowed from Latin radiatio, radiationis. By surface analysis, radiate + -ion.

ex.en: It's evident that human behaviour is more dangerous for the environment than radiation.
ex.ja: 人間の行為が放射性物質よりも環境に危険だということは明らかです。

note.ja: radiate（放射する）+ -ion。ラテン語 radius（光線・車輪の輻（や））。「放射」。radio、ray と同じ。

en: An act of hitting; a blow, a hit.
An act of striking with a weapon; a blow.
To draw the horizontal line across the upright part (of the letter t).
Followed by out or through: to draw a line or lines through (text) to indicate that it is deleted; to cancel, to strike or strike out.

stroke.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English strok, stroke (“blow from a weapon, cut”), from Old English strāc, from Proto-West Germanic *straik, from Proto-Germanic *straikaz (“stroke”), from Proto-Indo-European *streyg- (“to rub, stroke; to shear; to strike”).
Sense 3.5.2.2 (“the oblique, slash, or virgule (‘/’)”) is a contraction of oblique stroke, a variant of oblique which was originally used in telegraphy.
The verb is derived from the noun.
Cognates
* German Streich (“stroke”)
* Middle Low German strēk (“stroke, trick, prank”)
* Scots strak, strake, straik (“blow, stroke”)

ex.en: I had a stroke last year.
ex.ja: 去年脳卒中を起こしました。

ex.en: The child is stroking a cat.
ex.ja: 子供が猫を撫でている。

ex.en: What a stroke of luck!
ex.ja: なんて幸運なんだ。

note.ja: 古英語 strācian（なでる）と strīcan（打つ）から。「一撃・一筆・ひとかき」→ 突然襲う「脳卒中」→ 優しく「なでる」。strike と同系。

en: Having an effect that stuns.
Exceptionally beautiful or attractive.
The act by which a person or animal is physically stunned.

stunning.ety: From Middle English stunnyng, stunnynge, stounyng, equivalent to stun + -ing.

ex.en: The view is stunning.
ex.ja: 見事な景色だ。

note.ja: stun（気絶させる）+ -ing。「気絶させるほどの」→「驚くほど美しい」。astonish と同系。

en: A melody.
A song, or short musical composition.
To adjust (a musical instrument) so that it produces the correct pitches.
To adjust or modify (especially a mechanical or electrical device) so that it functions optimally.

tune.ety: From Middle English tune, an unexplained variant of tone, from Old French ton, from Latin tonus, from Ancient Greek τόνος (tónos, “a tone”). Doublet of tone, ton, and tonus.

ex.en: This tune is quite familiar to us all.
ex.ja: この曲は我々の誰にも良く知られている。

ex.en: I can't remember the tune of that song.
ex.ja: 私はあの歌のメロディーが思い出せない。

ex.en: The tune was not familiar to me.
ex.ja: わたしはその曲をしらなかった。

note.ja: tone（音）の変化形。「曲・旋律」→「調律する・（チャンネルを）合わせる」。

en: The state or condition of being useful; usefulness.
Something that is useful.
Having to do with, or owned by, a service provider.
containing or intended for any of a building’s often-utility-related commodity transport, such as pipes or wires, or converting equipment…

utility.ety: From Middle English utilite, from Old French utilite, utilitet (“usefulness”), from Latin ūtilitās, from uti (“to use”). By surface analysis, utile + -ity.

ex.en: Public utility charges will go up next April.
ex.ja: ４月から公共料金が値上げになる。

ex.en: We expect rapid growth of the utilities sector.
ex.ja: 公益事業部門の急成長を見込んでいます。

ex.en: You have to pay for utilities.
ex.ja: 諸設備の費用は払っていただきます。

note.ja: ラテン語 utilitas（有用性）から。uti（使う）。「有用性」→ 生活に役立つ「公共事業」。use と同じ。

en: Any craft designed for transportation on or in water, such as a ship, boat, or submarine.
A craft designed for transportation through air or space.
To put into a vessel.

ex.en: The port is filled with vessels of all kinds.
ex.ja: その港には色々な種類の船がある。

ex.en: A blood vessel broke in my eye.
ex.ja: 目の血管が切れてしまった。

ex.en: Empty vessels make the most sound.
ex.ja: 頭の空っぽな者ほど良くしゃべる。

note.ja: ラテン語 vascellum（小さな器）から。vas（器）。「器」→「船」→ 血を入れる器「血管」。vase と同じ。

en: Any plant unwanted at the place where and at the time when it is growing.
Cannabis.
To remove unwanted vegetation from a cultivated area (especially grass).
To pilfer the best items from a collection.

From Middle English weed, weod, from Old English wēod (“weed”), from Proto-West Germanic *weud (“weed”).

ex.en: Many weeds were growing among the flowers.
ex.ja: 花の間に多くの雑草が生えていた。

ex.en: You should get rid of these weeds.
ex.ja: この雑草は取り除いた方がいい。

ex.en: We have to get rid of weeds.
ex.ja: 雑草を取らなくてはならない。

note.ja: 古英語 wēod から。「雑草」→（俗）マリファナ。

In, at or to any place that one likes or chooses.
Regardless of the place in, at or to which.
In, at or to any place (that); anywhere.

note.ja: where + ever。「どこへ〜しても」。

en: The act or process of acquiring.
The thing acquired or gained; a gain.

acquisition.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French acquisicion, from Latin acquisītiō, from acquīrō, acquīrere; equivalent to acquire + -ition.

ex.en: Matt is a powerful acquisition for our team.
ex.ja: マットは我々のチームの強力な新メンバーだ。

ex.en: This is the latest acquisition to my library.
ex.ja: これがごく最近私の蔵書に加わった本です。

note.ja: ac（〜へ）+ quis（求める）+ ition。求めて手に入れること →「獲得・買収・習得」。

ex.en: Would you still be studying Japanese if it weren't for anime?
ex.ja: 日本語を学ぶ動機にやっぱりアニメは欠かせないよな？

note.ja: animation（アニメーション）の日本での略語が英語に逆輸入されたもの。anim（命・魂）を吹き込んだ絵 →「（日本の）アニメ」。

en: Traditionally the third of the four seasons, when deciduous trees lose their leaves, and temperatures and daylight hours decrease; typica…
The time period when someone or something is past its prime.
To spend the autumn (in a particular place).
To (cause to) undergo the changes associated with autumn, such as leaves changing color and falling from trees.

autumn.ety: Inherited from Middle English autumpne, from Middle French automne, from Old French automne, autonne, from Latin autumnus. Some of the verbal senses are from Latin autumnāre.

ex.en: It looks as if autumn is really here.
ex.ja: もうすっかり秋めいてきました。

ex.en: Autumn came and the leaves started to fall.
ex.ja: 秋になり、木の葉が落ち始めた。

ex.en: The leaves fall to the ground in autumn.
ex.ja: 秋には木の葉が地面に落ちる。

note.ja: ラテン語 autumnus から。語源ははっきりしない。アメリカでは fall も使う。

en: Courageous; daring.
Visually striking; conspicuous.
To make (a font or some text) bold.

bold.ety:
From Middle English bold, bolde, bald, beald, from Old English bald, beald (“bold, brave, confident, strong, of good courage, presumptuous, impudent”), from Proto-West Germanic *balþ, from Proto-Germanic *balþaz (“strong, bold”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel-, *bʰlē- (“to bloat, swell, bubble”).
Cognate with Dutch boud (“bold, courageous, fearless”), Middle High German balt (“bold”) (whence German bald (“soon”)), Swedish båld (“bold, dauntless”). Perhaps related to Albanian ballë (“forehead”) and Old Prussian balo (“forehead”). Compare typologically Italian affrontare (“to face, to deal with

ex.en: He made bold to speak to the King.
ex.ja: 彼は大胆にも王様に話し掛けた。

ex.en: It is bold of him to refuse our offer.
ex.ja: 私たちの申し出を断るとは大胆だ。

ex.en: We need somebody with bold new ideas.
ex.ja: 私達は大胆で新しい考え方をする人が必要だ。

note.ja: 古英語 beald（勇敢な）から。「大胆な」→ はっきり目立つ「太字の」。

en: Of or relating to the first class or rank, especially in literature or art.
Of or pertaining to established principles in a discipline.
One that is classical in some way; for example, a classical economist.

classical.ety: See classic § Etymology for history. By surface analysis, class + -ical or classic + -al or class + -ic + -al

ex.en: Classical music is not my cup of tea.
ex.ja: クラシック音楽は僕の好みじゃない。

ex.en: He is a man with a classical education.
ex.ja: 彼は古典の教育を受けている。

ex.en: She is a woman with a classical education.
ex.ja: 彼女は古典の教育を受けている。

note.ja: classic + -al。「古典的な」→ 音楽の「クラシックの」。

en: Sorted into classes or categories.
Formally assigned by a government to one of several levels of sensitivity, usually (in English) top secret, secret, confidential, and, in…
A classified advertisement in a newspaper or magazine.

ex.en: These can be classified roughly into three types.
ex.ja: これらは３つのタイプに大別される。

ex.en: Student part-time workers? Are those classified as employed?
ex.ja: 学生アルバイトって、有職者に分類されるのだろうか？

ex.en: The librarian classified the books according to subject.
ex.ja: 司書は主題によって本を分類した。

note.ja: classify（分類する）+ -ed。「分類された」→ 機密に分類された「機密の」→ 新聞の「分類広告」。

en: To grip tightly.
To fasten with a clip.
Something which clips or grasps; a device for attaching one object to another.
An unspecified, but normally understood as rapid, speed or pace.

clip.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gel-
Proto-Indo-European *b(ʰ)
Proto-Indo-European *gelb(ʰ)-der.
Proto-Germanic *klupjaną
Old English clyppan
Middle English clippen
English clip
From Middle English clippen, cleppen, clüppen, from Old English clyppan (“to hug, embrace, cherish, clasp”), from Proto-Germanic *klumpijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *glemb-, *glembʰ- (“lump, clump, clod, clamp”). Cognate with Old Frisian kleppa, klippa (“to hug, embrace”), Middle High German klimpen, klimpfen (“to contract tightly, constrict, squeeze”).

ex.en: I clipped some articles out of the newspaper.
ex.ja: 新聞から記事を切り抜いた。

ex.en: I have a newspaper clipping file.
ex.ja: 新聞をまとめておくファイルを持っている。

ex.en: Do you have a paper clip?
ex.ja: クリップ持ってる？

note.ja: 「切り取る」は古北欧語 klippa から。「留める・クリップ」は古英語 clyppan（抱く）からで別語。動画の「一部」は切り取ったもの。

en: A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle.
A token used in a special establishment like a casino.
To make of a definite fineness, and convert into coins, as a mass of metal.
To make or fabricate (especially a word or phrase).

coin.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin cuneusder.
Old French coinbor.
Middle English coyn
English coin
From Middle English coyn, from Old French coigne (“wedge, cornerstone, die for stamping”), from Latin cuneus (“wedge”). Doublet of coign and cuneus. See also quoin (“cornerstone”). Displaced Middle English mynt, from Old English mynet (whence modern English mint), which was derived from Latin monēta.

ex.en: Where did you pick up those old coins?
ex.ja: あの古いコインをどこで手に入れたのか。

ex.en: Look at this old coin you have here.
ex.ja: あなたがここで手にしている古いこのコインを見てご覧なさい。

ex.en: He took out a coin from his pocket.
ex.ja: 彼は、ポケットからコインを取りだした。

note.ja: 古フランス語 coin（くさび・打ち型）から。ラテン語 cuneus（くさび）。打ち型で打った「硬貨」→ 新語を「作る」。

en: An agreement or arrangement between multiple parties to do something harmful, immoral or subversive; an instance of collusion.
An agreement between two or more persons to break the law at some time in the future.

conspiracy.ety: From Middle English conspiracie, from Anglo-Norman conspiracie, from Latin cōnspīrātiō. By surface analysis, conspire + -acy.

ex.en: To be frank, I think this 'conspiracy theory' is nonsense.
ex.ja: ハッキリ言って、この「陰謀説」はナンセンスだと思う。

ex.en: Without a moment's hesitation, they took drastic action against the conspiracy.
ex.ja: ためらうことなく、その陰謀にたいする徹底した対抗処置をとった。

ex.en: Many conspiracy theorists leverage unverifiable statements and claim them as facts.
ex.ja: 多くの陰謀論者が、未検証な発言を利用してそれらを事実と主張する。

note.ja: con（共に）+ spir（息をする）+ acy。一緒に息を合わせること →（ひそかに示し合わせる）→「陰謀」。

en: A debate or discussion of opposing opinions; (generally) strife.

controversy.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ḱe?
Proto-Indo-European *ḱóm
Proto-Italic *kom
Proto-Italic *kom-
Proto-Indo-European *-teros
Proto-Italic *-teros
Proto-Italic *komterosder.
Proto-Italic *komterād
Latin contrā
Proto-Indo-European *wert-
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Indo-European *wr̥ttós
Proto-Italic *worssosder.
Latin vorsus
Latin versus
Latin contrōversus
Proto-Indo-European *-(i)yós
Proto-Italic *-ijos
Proto-Italic *-ios
Old Latin -ios
Latin -ius
Latin -ia
Latin contrōversia
Old French controversiebor.
Middle English controversie
English controversy
From Middle English controversie,

ex.en: The question excited much controversy.
ex.ja: その問題はいろいろな論争を呼んだ。

ex.en: There was a controversy about the location of the new school.
ex.ja: 新しい学校の建設地については論争があった。

ex.en: His bold plan gave rise to much controversy.
ex.ja: 彼の大胆な計画は大きな論争を巻き起こした。

note.ja: contro（反対に）+ vers（向ける）+ y。反対の方へ向き合うこと →「論争」。

en: To vanish.
To go missing; to become a missing person.

disappear.ety:
From Middle English disapeeren, equivalent to dis- + appear. Displaced native Old English fordwīnan.
Displaced native Old English cwincan, whose causative persists as quench (“put out (fire)”).

ex.en: After 6 p.m. the employees began to disappear.
ex.ja: ６時を過ぎると従業員は帰り始めた。

ex.en: All the snow on the mountain has disappeared.
ex.ja: 山の雪がすっかり消えた。

ex.en: He did not pay the debt and disappeared.
ex.ja: 彼は借金を踏み倒して姿を暗ました。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ appear（現れる）。「消える」。

en: To meet (someone) or find (something), especially unexpectedly.
To confront (someone or something) face to face.
A meeting, especially one that is unplanned or unexpected.
A hostile, often violent meeting; a confrontation, skirmish, or clash, as between combatants.

encounter.ety: From Middle English encountren, from Anglo-Norman encountrer, Old French encontrer (“to confront”), from encontre (“against, counter to”), from Late Latin incontrā (“in front of”) itself from Latin in (“in”) + contrā (“against”).

ex.en: In spring, I look forward to many encounters!
ex.ja: 春には、たくさんの出会いが待っている！

ex.en: He encountered a friend on the road.
ex.ja: 彼は道で友人と出くわした。

ex.en: It's the first time he has encountered people speaking French.
ex.ja: 彼のフランス語との最初の出会いなのです。

note.ja: 古フランス語 encontrer から。en + contre（〜に向かって）。「向かい合う」→「出会う」。counter、contra と同じ。

en: The fact of being equal.
The fact of being equal, of having the same value.

equality.ety: Borrowed from Middle French equalité (modern French égalité), from Latin aequālitās, aequālitātem. Doublet of equity. By surface analysis, equal + -ity

ex.en: He was in favor of equality for all.
ex.ja: 彼は全ての人が平等であることに賛成した。

ex.en: Women want equality of opportunity with men.
ex.ja: 女性は男性との機会の平等を要求している。

ex.en: Women have achieved equality in some areas.
ex.ja: 女性はある分野では平等を達成してきた。

note.ja: equ（等しい）+ al + ity。等しいこと →「平等」。

en: Shortened form of examine

ex.en: I was busy studying for the term exam.
ex.ja: 期末試験の勉強で忙しかったのです。

ex.en: If you work hard, you'll pass your exam.
ex.ja: 一生懸命勉強すれば試験に受かるでしょう。

ex.en: Tom worked hard only to fail the exam.
ex.ja: トムは一生懸命に勉強したのに試験に落ちた。

note.ja: examination の短縮。ラテン語 examen（天秤の針）。「量って調べる」→「試験」。

en: The act of examining.
Particularly, an inspection by a medical professional to establish the extent and nature of any sickness or injury.

examination.ety: From Middle English examinacioun, from Old French examinacion, from Latin exāminātiō. Morphologically examine + -ation.

ex.en: You may as well prepare for your examination.
ex.ja: 君は試験の準備をしたほうがよい。

ex.en: To my joy, my daughter passed the examination.
ex.ja: 嬉しいことに娘が試験に合格した。

ex.en: To her joy, she passed the entrance examination.
ex.ja: 嬉しいことに、彼女は入試に合格した。

note.ja: examine（調べる）+ -ation。ラテン語 examen（天秤の針）。「試験・検査・診察」。exam はその短縮。

en: An act of joining together into a single political entity.
An array of nations or states that are unified under one central authority.
Of an architectural style popular around the time of federation.

federation.ety: Borrowed from French fédération, from Late Latin foederatio, from Latin foederare; equivalent to federate + -ion.

ex.en: The national tennis federation chose her for the team.
ex.ja: 全国テニス連盟は彼女を代表チームに選んだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 foedus（同盟・契約）から。信頼で結ばれた連合 →「連邦・連盟」。fid（信頼）と同じ祖先 *bʰeydʰ-。

en: Related to the treasury of a country, company, region or city, particularly to government spending and revenue.
Pertaining to finance and money in general; financial.
A public official in certain countries having control of public revenue.
Procurator fiscal, a public prosecutor.

fiscal.ety: From Middle French fiscal, from Latin fiscus (“treasury”) – see fiscus and fisc.

ex.en: The scholar is an authority on fiscal policy.
ex.ja: その学者は財政政策の権威である。

ex.en: Developing countries suffer from difficulties of fiscal problems.
ex.ja: 発展途上国は財政問題で諸々の困難に苦しんでいる。

ex.en: They labored over the budget for the fiscal year 1997.
ex.ja: 彼らは苦労して１９９７会計年度の予算を作成した。

note.ja: ラテン語 fiscus（かご・国庫）から。「国庫の」→「財政の・会計の」。confiscate（没収する）と同じ。

en: Someone who guards, watches over, or protects.
A person legally responsible for a minor (in loco parentis).

guardian.ety: From Middle English gardein, garden, (also wardein, > Modern English warden), from Old French guardein, from the verb guarder, of Germanic origin. Compare French gardien. Doublet of warden. By surface analysis, guard + -ian.

ex.en: I regard myself as your guardian.
ex.ja: 私はきみの保護者のつもりだ。

ex.en: Minors must have a parent or guardian sign the form.
ex.ja: 未成年の方は、保護者のサインをもらってください。

ex.en: John acts like Helen's guardian.
ex.ja: ジョンはヘレンの保護者のようにふるまっている。

note.ja: guard（守る）+ -ian。「保護者・守護者」。warden と同じ語源。

en: Lacking a permanent place of residence.
Containing no place that might be called home.

homeless.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ḱey-
Proto-Indo-European *-mos
Proto-Indo-European *ḱóymos
Proto-Indo-European *teḱ-
Proto-Indo-European *-éyti
Proto-Indo-European *tḱéytibf.
Proto-Indo-European *tḱey-
Proto-Indo-European *-mos
Proto-Indo-European *tḱóymos
Proto-Germanic *haimaz
Proto-West Germanic *haim
Old English hām
Proto-Indo-European *lewh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *lewHs-der.

Proto-Germanic *-lausaz
Proto-West Germanic *-laus
Old English -lēas
Old English hāmlēas
Middle English *homles
English homeless
From Middle English *homles, *hamles,

ex.en: Those homeless people are living hand-to-mouth.
ex.ja: ホームレスのあの人たちはその日暮らしです。

ex.en: I gave some money to the homeless.
ex.ja: ホームレスにお金を恵んであげました。

ex.en: She told me she was homeless.
ex.ja: 彼女はホームレスだと言われた。

note.ja: home（家）+ -less。「家のない」。

en: The action of intervening; interfering in some course of events.
A legal motion through which a person or entity who has not been named as a party to a case seeks to have the court order that they be ma…

intervention.ety: From Middle French intervention, from Latin interventiō. Morphologically intervene + -tion.

ex.en: Quick intervention by the doctor saved his life.
ex.ja: 医師がすぐに処置したことで彼の命は救われた。

note.ja: inter（間に）+ vent（来る）+ ion。間に割って入ること →「介入・干渉」。

en: One who loves and cares for another person in a romantic way; a sweetheart, love, soulmate, boyfriend, girlfriend, or spouse.
A sexual partner, especially one with whom someone is having an affair.

lover.ety: From Middle English lovere, luffer, lufere, equivalent to love + -er.

ex.en: The two lovers sat face to face, drinking tea.
ex.ja: ２人の恋人は差し向かいに座ってお茶を飲んでいた。

ex.en: He is a great lover of music.
ex.ja: 彼は音楽がとっても好きだ。

ex.en: He's what society calls a real lover of music.
ex.ja: 彼は世間でいう音楽の真の愛好者だ。

note.ja: love（愛する）+ -er。「恋人・愛好家」。

en: Used or accepted broadly rather than by small portions of population, market, scientific community, etc.
The principal current in a flow, such as a river or flow of air
That which is common; the norm.
To popularize, to normalize, to render mainstream.
To become mainstream.

mainstream.ety: From main + stream. Cognate with Icelandic meginstraumur (“a main current, mainstream”).

ex.en: Electric cars are becoming mainstream.
ex.ja: 電気自動車が主流になりつつある。

note.ja: main（主な）+ stream（流れ）。「本流」→「主流」。

en: The details of the food to be served at a banquet; a bill of fare.
A list containing the food and beverages served at a restaurant, café, or bar. Menus may be printed on paper sheets provided to customers…

menu.ety: Borrowed from French menu. Doublet of menudo and minute.

ex.en: This isn't what was written on the menu.
ex.ja: これはメニューに書かれてあった内容とちがっています。

ex.en: Do you have any questions about the menu?
ex.ja: 料理について何か質問がありますか。

ex.en: Can I have the menu again, please?
ex.ja: もう一度メニューを見せていただけますか。

note.ja: フランス語 menu（細かい・詳細な）から。ラテン語 minutus（小さくされた）。「料理の細目」→「献立」。minute（細かい）と同じ。

en: Having the same relationship, each to each other.
Collective, done or held in common.
A mutual fund.
A mutual organization.

mutual.ety: Borrowed from Middle French mutuel, from Latin mūtuus. Displaced native Old English ġemǣne.

ex.en: They gave mutual help to each other.
ex.ja: 彼らは相互に助け合った。

ex.en: Forget it. He is our mutual friend, after all.
ex.ja: やめろよ。あいつは俺たちの友達だろ。

ex.en: It's necessary that we come to a mutual understanding.
ex.ja: 我々の相互理解が必要である。

note.ja: ラテン語 mutuus（交換された）から。mut（変える・交換する）。互いに交わし合う →「相互の・共通の」。

en: A crime or sin.
An affront, injury, or insult.

offense.ety: From Middle English offence, from Old French offense, from Latin offensa (“a striking against; displeasure; injury”).

ex.en: He committed an offense against our laws.
ex.ja: 彼は我が国の法律に違反した。

ex.en: The most effective defense is offense.
ex.ja: 最も効果的な防御は攻撃である。

ex.en: He is quick to take offense.
ex.ja: 彼は直に腹を立てる。

note.ja: ラテン語 offensa（つまずき・攻撃）から。ob + fendere（打つ）。「打ちかかること」→「攻撃・違反・感情を害すること」。offend と同じ。

en: Relating to the mouth.
Done or taken by the mouth.
A spoken test or examination, particularly in a language class.
A physical examination of the mouth.

oral.ety:
PIE word
 *h₁óh₃s
Early 17th century borrowing from Late Latin ōrālis, from ōs (“the mouth”) + -ālis (“-al”, adjectival suffix).

ex.en: She gave an oral report to her boss.
ex.ja: 彼女は上司に口頭で報告をした。

ex.en: His oral agreement may not mean anything without his signed contract.
ex.ja: 彼が署名した契約書がなければ、彼の口頭での同意は何の意味もないだろう。

ex.en: She had an oral examination in English.
ex.ja: 彼女は英語の口頭試験を受けた。

note.ja: ラテン語 os（口）から。oris。「口の・口頭の」。

en: Of fear, fright, etc: overwhelming or sudden.
Pertaining to or resulting from overwhelming fear or fright.
Overwhelming fear or fright, often affecting groups of people or animals; (countable) an instance of this; a fright, a scare.
A rapid reduction in asset prices due to broad efforts to raise cash in anticipation of such prices continuing to decline.
To cause (someone) to feel panic (“overwhelming fear or fright”); also, to frighten (someone) into acting hastily.
To cause (a computer system) to crash.

panic.ety:
The adjective is borrowed from Middle French panique, a word itself borrowed from Ancient Greek πανικός (panikós, “pertaining to Pan”); Pan, the Greek god of fields and woods, was believed to be the source of mysterious sounds that caused contagious, groundless fear in herds and crowds, or in people in lonely spots.
Adjective sense 3 (“pertaining to or resulting from overpowering fear or fright”) is partly an attributive use of the noun.
The noun is derived from the adjective, while the verb is derived from the noun. Verb sense 1.3 (“to highly amuse, entertain, or impress (an audience watching

ex.en: The fire caused a panic in the theater.
ex.ja: 火事で劇場の中は大混乱になった。

ex.en: There's no need to panic. There's plenty of time.
ex.ja: そんなにあわてることはないよ。時間はたっぷりあるんだから。

ex.en: There's no reason to panic. Just handle it quickly.
ex.ja: オタオタしてないで、はやくその問題を解決しなさい！

note.ja: ギリシャ語 panikos（牧神パンの）から。パンの神が人や家畜に突然の恐怖を起こすと信じられたことから。

en: To follow urgently, originally with intent to capture or harm; to chase.
To follow, travel down (a particular way, course of action etc.).

pursue.ety: From Middle English pursuen, from Anglo-Norman pursure, poursuire etc., from Latin prōsequor (though influenced by persequor). Doublet of prosecute.

ex.en: She is pursuing her career in interior design.
ex.ja: 彼女はインテリア・デザインの仕事をしていきたいと考えている。

ex.en: Students often pursue their teacher with questions.
ex.ja: 学生はしばしば先生を質問攻めにする。

ex.en: I plan to pursue a career in international finance.
ex.ja: 国際金融で仕事を続けるつもりです。

note.ja: 古フランス語 poursuir から。ラテン語 prosequi ＝ pro（前へ）+ sequi（追う）。「追い求める」。pursuit、prosecute と同じ。

en: A person seeking refuge (as for shelter or protection), especially in a foreign country, out of fear or prospect of political, religious …
To convey (slaves) away from the advance of the federal forces.

refugee.ety: From French réfugié, past participle of réfugier (“to take refuge, to seek refuge”), from Old French refuge (“hiding place”) from Latin refugium (“a place of refuge, place to flee back to”), originally describing French Huguenots fleeing religious persecution after the revocation of the Edict of Nantes in 1685. Noun sense 1 was "one seeking asylum" until 1914, when it evolved to mean more generally "one fleeing home" (first applied in this sense to civilians in Flanders heading west to escape fighting in World War I). By surface analysis, refuge + -ee. Displaced native Old English flīema.

ex.en: They established a Japanese language class for the refugees.
ex.ja: 彼らは難民たちのために日本語の授業を設立した。

ex.en: Refugees in Africa are seeking help.
ex.ja: アフリカの難民が救いを求めている。

ex.en: That church organization takes in refugees.
ex.ja: あの教会施設は避難民を収容している。

note.ja: フランス語 réfugié（避難した）から。ラテン語 refugere ＝ re + fugere（逃げる）。refuge（避難所）、fugitive と同じ。

en: To divide or separate the parts of (especially something flimsy, such as paper or fabric), by cutting or tearing; to tear off or out by v…
To tear apart; to rapidly become two parts.
A tear (in paper, etc.).
A rip current: a strong outflow of surface water, away from the shore, that returns water from incoming waves.

rip.ety:
From Middle English rippen, from earlier ryppen (“to pluck”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *rupjaną and/or *ruppōną, intensive of *raupijaną, causative of Proto-Indo-European *Hrewp- (“to break”). Possible doublet of rub.

An event that is not, or cannot be, foreseen.
To undertake a risky or daring journey.
To risk or offer.

ex.ja: 諺にもある通り「虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず」だ。

ex.ja: 会社はその事業に資本参加した。

Compare also German Low German Brickje (“small board, tray”). Related to break.
The social media slang sense derives from memes about building up one's feed “brick by brick”, analogizing bricks with reels that inform the algorithm.
The sense of a helpful, reliable person comes from Lycurgus referring to the army as the wal

ex.ja: 彼は一人でこの寂しい場所に住んでいます。

ex.en: He is a lonely man with few friends.
ex.ja: 彼は友達がほとんどいない孤独な人だ。

ex.en: I was lonely, with nobody to play with.
ex.ja: 遊び相手がなくて孤独だった。

note.ja: lone（ひとりの）+ -ly。lone は alone の短縮。「孤独な」。

en: Relenting; forbearance to cause or allow harm to another.
Forgiveness or compassion, especially toward those less fortunate.
To feel mercy
To show mercy; to pardon or treat leniently because of mercy
Expressing surprise or alarm.

mercy.ety: From Middle English mercy, merci, from Anglo-Norman merci (compare continental Old French merci, mercit), from Latin mercēs (“wages, fee, price”), from merx (“wares, merchandise”). Displaced native Old English mildheortnes (literally "mildheartedness"). Cognate with French merci, whence the doublet merci.

ex.en: Man is indeed at the mercy of nature.
ex.ja: 人間は実際自然のなすがままである。

ex.en: Beer sales are at the mercy of the weather.
ex.ja: ビールの売れ行きは天候しだいです。

ex.en: The ship was at the mercy of the waves.
ex.ja: 船は波に翻弄されていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 merces（報酬）から。天国での「報い」→「慈悲」。merchant と同じ merc。

en: In spite of what preceded; yet.

nevertheless.ety: From Middle English nevertheles, never-þe-les, nevere-þe-lesse. By surface analysis, never (“not at all”) + the + less; compare never the wiser.

ex.en: Nevertheless, I want to go there.
ex.ja: それでも、そこに行ってみたい。

ex.en: We thought it would rain; nevertheless, we started on our trip.
ex.ja: 雨が降るだろうと思っていたのだが、それでも旅行に出かけた。

ex.en: I was very tired, but I was nevertheless unable to sleep.
ex.ja: 私は疲れていたが、それにもかかわらず眠れなかった。

note.ja: never（決して〜ない）+ the（それだけ）+ less（少なく）。「それだけ少なくなることはない」→「それにもかかわらず」。

en: The chemical element (symbol O) with an atomic number of 8 and relative atomic mass of 15.9994. It is a colorless and odorless gas. Somet…
Molecular oxygen (O₂), a colorless, odorless gas at room temperature.

oxygen.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ-der.?
Ancient Greek ὀξύς (oxús)
Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *-os
Proto-Indo-European *ǵénh₁os
Proto-Hellenic *génos
Ancient Greek γένος (génos)
French oxygènebor.
English oxygen
Borrowed from French oxygène (originally in the form principe oxygène, a variant of principe oxigine ‘acidifying principle’, suggested by Lavoisier), from Ancient Greek ὀξύς (oxús, “sharp”) + γένος (génos, “birth”), referring to oxygen's supposed role in the formation of acids. By surface analysis, oxy- + -gen.

ex.en: Plants give off oxygen as they make food.
ex.ja: 植物は栄養物を作っているとき、酸素を放出する。

ex.en: No living things could live without oxygen.
ex.ja: 生物は酸素なしでは生きられない。

ex.en: You cannot burn anything without oxygen.
ex.ja: 酸素がないと何も燃やせない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 oxys（鋭い・酸っぱい）+ gen（生む）。「酸を生むもの」と考えられて名付けられた →「酸素」。hydrogen（水を生むもの→水素）も同じ gen。

en: A wind instrument consisting of a tube, often lined with holes to allow for adjustment in pitch, sounded by blowing into the tube.
A tube used to produce sound in an organ; an organ pipe.
To play (music) on a pipe instrument, such as a bagpipe or a flute.
To shout loudly and at high pitch.

pipe.ety:
From Middle English pīpe, pype (“hollow cylinder or tube used as a conduit or container; duct or vessel of the body; musical instrument; financial records maintained by the English Exchequer, pipe roll”), from Old English pīpe (“pipe (musical instrument); the channel of a small stream”), from Proto-West Germanic *pīpā. Reinforced by Vulgar Latin *pīpa, from Latin pipire, pipiare, pipare, from pīpiō (“to chirp, peep”), of imitative origin. Displaced native Old English fealh and Old English þrūh. Doublet of fife.
Cognate with Dutch pijp, German Pfeife, Danish pibe, Norwegian Bokmål and Norwegian

ex.en: He spoke with a pipe in his mouth.
ex.ja: 彼はパイプをくわえて話した。

ex.en: The pipe shop is across the street.
ex.ja: パイプ屋は通りの向こう側です。

ex.en: The oil ran through a thick pipe.
ex.ja: 石油が太いパイプの中を流れた。

note.ja: ラテン語 pipa（笛）から。pipare（ピーピー鳴く）。擬音的な語。「笛」→「管」。

piss.ety: From Middle English pisse (noun) and pissen (verb), from Old French pissier, possibly from Vulgar Latin *pīssiāre, probably of imitative origin. Compare Old Norse pissa (“to urinate, piss”). Displaced Old English miċġe (“urine”) and mīgan (“to urinate”).

ex.en: I'm dying for a piss.
ex.ja: オシッコが漏れそう。

ex.en: You piss me off!
ex.ja: 君は僕をいらいらさせる。

ex.en: I've got work to do, so piss off and leave me alone.
ex.ja: 仕事があるんで、さっさと出てって僕を一人にしてくれないかな。

note.ja: 古フランス語 pissier から。擬音的な卑語。

en: A literary piece written in verse.
A piece of writing in the tradition of poetry, an instance of poetry.

poem.ety: From Middle French poème, from Latin poēma, from Ancient Greek ποίημα (poíēma), from ποιέω (poiéō, “to make”). Widely displaced English leed.

ex.en: This poem was written by him last night.
ex.ja: この詩は昨夜彼によって書かれました。

ex.en: We had to learn the poem by heart.
ex.ja: 私たちはその詩を暗記しなければならなかった。

ex.en: He gave us his impression of the poem.
ex.ja: 彼はその詩の感想を述べた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 poiēma（作られたもの）から。poiein（作る）。poet、poetry と同じ。

en: The fine particles which are the result of reducing a dry substance by pounding, grinding, or triturating, or the result of decay; dust.
A mixture of fine dry, sweet-smelling particles applied to the face or other body parts, to reduce shine or to alleviate chaffing.
To reduce to fine particles; to pound, grind, or rub into a powder.
To sprinkle with powder, or as if with powder.

powder.ety: From Middle English poudre, pouder, pouldre, borrowed from Old French poudre, poldre, puldre, from Latin pulverem, accusative singular of Latin pulvis (“dust, powder”). Doublet of pulver. Compare pollen (“fine flour”), polverine, pulverize.

ex.en: You have to take this powder after each meal.
ex.ja: この粉薬は毎食後飲んでください。

ex.en: The Middle East is still called a powder keg.
ex.ja: 中東は今でも危険な火薬庫と呼ばれている。

ex.en: I think I shall go to the powder room for a moment.
ex.ja: ちょっと、トイレ行ってこようっと。

note.ja: ラテン語 pulvis（ちり・粉）から古フランス語を経た語。「粉」。

en: The belief that there are distinct human races with inherent differences which determine their abilities, and generally that some are sup…
The policies, practices, or systems (e.g. government or political) promoting this belief or promoting the dominance of one or more races …

racism.ety: Borrowed from French racisme, equivalent to race + -ism.

ex.en: The school teaches students to stand up against racism.
ex.ja: その学校は人種差別に立ち向かうよう生徒に教えている。

note.ja: race（人種）+ -ism。「人種差別」。

en: Lacking in refinement or civility; bad-mannered; discourteous.
Lacking refinement or skill; untaught; ignorant; raw.

rude.ety: From Middle English rude, from Old French rude, ruide, from Latin rudis (“rough, raw, rude, wild, untilled”).

ex.en: It is rude of you to say so.
ex.ja: そんなことを言うのは失礼よ。

ex.en: Nothing can excuse him for such rude behavior.
ex.ja: この様な彼の無礼な行為はどんなことがあっても許されない。

ex.en: Don't take any notice of those rude boys.
ex.ja: あんな不作法な少年たちのことなど気に留めるな。

note.ja: ラテン語 rudis（粗い・未熟な）から。「粗野な」→「失礼な」。rudiment（基礎）と同じ。

en: A simple machine, a helical inclined plane.
A (usually) metal fastener consisting of a partially or completely threaded shank, sometimes with a threaded point, and a head used to bo…
To connect or assemble pieces using a screw.
To extort or practice extortion upon; to oppress by unreasonable or extortionate exactions; to put the screws on.

screw.ety:

From Middle English screw, scrue (“screw”); apparently, despite the difference in meaning, from Old French escroue (“nut, cylindrical socket, screwhole”), from Latin scrōfa (“female pig”) through comparison with the corkscrew shape of a pig's penis. There is also the Old French escruve (“screw”), from Old Dutch *scrūva ("screw"; whence Middle Dutch schruyve (“screw”)), which probably influenced or conflated with the aforementioned, resulting in th

ex.en: He seems like he's got a few screws loose.
ex.ja: 彼は風変わりな奴だ。

ex.en: When I turned the screw, water burst out.
ex.ja: 僕がネジを回すと水が吹き出してきた。

ex.en: I screwed up my courage and went there.
ex.ja: 私は思い切ってそこに行った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 escroue（ナット）から。ラテン語 scrofa（雌豚）とされる（豚のしっぽのねじれから）。

en: The ordinal form of the number seven.
The person or thing in the seventh position.
One of seven equal parts of a whole.

seventh.ety: From Middle English seventhe, sefte, from Old English seofoþa, from Proto-West Germanic *sebundō, from Proto-Germanic *sebundô. The -n-, lost in northern Proto-West Germanic, was later reinserted by analogy with seven, equivalent to seven + -th.

ex.en: We arrived on the morning of the seventh.
ex.ja: 私たちは７日の朝到着した。

ex.en: The seventh day of the week is Saturday.
ex.ja: 週の７番目の日は土曜日です。

ex.en: India is the seventh largest country in the world.
ex.ja: インドは世界で７番目に大きい国である。

note.ja: seven の序数。

en: A place where a person or animal may find protection from the elements (especially rain, storms, or cold) sometimes as a place to sleep (…
A bare-bones above-ground structure meant to provide temporary cover from the elements; usually small and with no door to close.
To provide cover from damage or harassment; to shield; to protect.
To take cover.

shelter.ety:
From Middle English sheltron, sheldtrume (“roof or wall formed by locked shields”), from Old English sċildtruma, sċyldtruma (“a phalanx, company (of troops), a tortoise, a covering, shed, shelter”, literally “shield-troop”), from sċyld, sċield (“shield”) + truma (“a troop of soldiers”). Cognate with Scots schilthrum, schiltrum. More at shield, and Old English trymman (“to strengthen”), from trum (“strong, firm”) at trim.
Doublet of sheltron (a kind of military formation), which is the more conservative of the two.

ex.en: Shelters have been built in fear of war.
ex.ja: 戦争を恐れてシェルターが作られてきた。

ex.en: I had to take shelter under a tree.
ex.ja: 木の下で雨宿りしなければなりませんでした。

ex.en: Food, clothing and shelter are the basis of life.
ex.ja: 衣食住は生活の基本です。

note.ja: shield（盾）+ troop（隊）の変化 scheltrum（盾で囲んだ隊形）からとされる。「保護するもの」→「避難所」。

en: A person's name, written by that person, used as identification or to signify approval of accompanying material, such as a legal contract.
An act of signing one's name; an act of producing a signature.
Distinctive, characteristic, indicative of identity.
To sign with one's signature, to write one's signature on.

signature.ety: Borrowed from Middle French signature, or from Medieval Latin signātūra, future active periphrastic of verb signāre from signum (“sign”), + -tūra, feminine of -tūrus, future active periphrastic suffix. Displaced native Old English handseten (literally “hand setting”).

ex.en: Please return one set to us with your signature.
ex.ja: 一通に署名の上ご返送ください。

ex.en: I attached my signature to the document.
ex.ja: 私は書類に署名した。

ex.en: May I have your signature here, please?
ex.ja: こちらにサインを頂けますでしょうか。

note.ja: sign（印）+ at + ure。自分の印をつけること →「署名」。

en: Any of various eight-legged, predatory arthropods, of the order Araneae, most of which spin webs to catch prey.
A float (drink) made by mixing ice-cream and a soda or fizzy drink (such as lemonade).
To move like a spider.
To cover a surface like a cobweb.

spider.ety:
Inherited from Middle English spithre, spider, from Old English spīþra (“spider”), from Proto-West Germanic *spinþrijō, from Proto-Germanic *spinnaną (“to spin”). Mostly displaced attercop (“spider, unpleasant person”), now a dialectal term.
Compare typologically Proto-Slavic *mězgyrь (whence Russian мизги́рь (mizgírʹ)) (akin to Latvian mežģīt), Turkish örümcek (akin to örmek).

ex.en: There are people that are afraid of spiders.
ex.ja: クモが怖い人もいる。

ex.en: In the living room there was a huge spider.
ex.ja: リビングに大きなクモがいたんだ。

ex.en: There was a huge spider in the living room.
ex.ja: リビングに大きなクモがいたんだ。

note.ja: 古英語 spīthra から。spin（糸を紡ぐ）+ -er。「糸を紡ぐもの」。

en: An acknowledgment of gratitude, respect or admiration; an accompanying gift.
An homage made in a body of work to another work or creator.
To pay (something) as tribute.

tribute.ety: From Middle English tribut (14th c.), from Middle French tribut, from Latin tributum (“tribute”, literally “a thing contributed or paid”), past participle of tribuere (“to assign, allot”), usually derived from tribus (whence English tribe).

ex.en: The verdict is a tribute to their fairness.
ex.ja: 評決は公平な審議の証拠である。

note.ja: ラテン語 tribuere（割り当てる・与える）から。割り当てて納めるもの →「貢ぎ物」→ 敬意として捧げるもの →「賛辞・敬意」。

en: A finger-operated lever used to fire a gun.
A similar device used to activate any mechanism.
To fire (a weapon); to set off or trip (a mechanism or function of a device).
To cause, to precipitate, to bring (something) about in response or as a result.

trigger.ety: Originally tricker, from Dutch trekker (“pull”, noun, as in drawer-pull, bell-pull), from Dutch trekken (“to drag, draw, pull”).

ex.en: I pulled the trigger again and again.
ex.ja: 私は連続で引き金を引いた。

ex.en: Police can't be trigger happy.
ex.ja: 警察は簡単に銃を使ってはいけない。

ex.en: Tom didn't have the courage to pull the trigger.
ex.ja: トムには引き金を引く勇気がなかった。

note.ja: オランダ語 trekker（引くもの）から。trekken（引く）。trek（旅）と同じ。「引き金」→「きっかけ」。

en: To change with time or a similar parameter.
To institute a change in, from a current state; to modify.

vary.ety: From Middle English varien, from Old French varier, from Latin variō (“to change, alter, make different”), from varius (“different, various”); see various.

ex.en: It includes widely varying organizations, people, and ideas.
ex.ja: これには、様々な種類の団体、人々、考え方が含まれている。

ex.en: Your philosophy of life varies from mine.
ex.ja: 君の人生観は僕のと違っているね。

ex.en: The price of gold varies from day to day.
ex.ja: 金の値段は日ごとに変わる。

note.ja: ラテン語 variare から。varius（さまざまな）。「変わる・異なる」。various、variety と同じ。

en: A theater, auditorium, arena, or other area designated for sporting or entertainment events.
A neighborhood or near place; the place or county in which anything is alleged to have happened; also, the place where an action is laid,…

venue.ety: From Middle English venu, from Old French venue, the feminine singular past participle of the verb venir (to come). Doublet of veny.

ex.en: The inside of the venue was silent.
ex.ja: 会場内は、シーンと静まり返っていました。

ex.en: At the venue, the scene was quiet.
ex.ja: 会場内は、シーンと静まり返っていました。

ex.en: What is your favourite music venue?
ex.ja: 一番好きな音楽会場ってどこ？

note.ja: 古フランス語 venue（来ること）から。venir（来る）。「人がやって来る場所」→「会場」。avenue、event と同じ ven。

en: A spontaneous abortion; a miscarriage.
An induced abortion.

abortion.ety: From Latin abortiōnem (“miscarriage, abortion”), from aborior (“to miscarry”). Equivalent to abort + -ion. Displaced native Old English ǣwyrp (literally “throwing out, rejection”).

ex.en: People are taking sides on the abortion issue.
ex.ja: 中絶問題で議論が二分しています。

ex.en: Are you for or against abortions?
ex.ja: あなたは妊娠中絶に賛成ですか、反対ですか。

ex.en: The independent candidate took the abortion issue off his platform.
ex.ja: その無所属候補者は中絶問題を公約からはずしました。

note.ja: abort（中止する）+ -ion。ラテン語 aboriri ＝ ab（離れて）+ oriri（生まれる・昇る）。「生まれずに終わる」→「妊娠中絶」。origin と同じ。

en: The state of being accurate; being free from error; exactness; correctness
Exact conformity to truth, or to a rule or model; degree of conformity of a measure to a true or standard value.

ex.en: Check up on the accuracy of this article.
ex.ja: この記事が何処まで本当か調べてくれ。

ex.en: I began to doubt the accuracy of his statement.
ex.ja: 私は彼の陳述の正確さを疑い始めた。

ex.en: He reported the details with accuracy.
ex.ja: 彼はその詳細を正確に報告した。

note.ja: accurate（正確な）+ -cy。ad + curare（注意する）。「注意を払った」→「正確さ」。cure、curious と同じ cur。

Insincere; fake, forced, or feigned.

ex.en: Artificial leather can't compare with the real thing.
ex.ja: 人造皮革は本物の皮にかなわない。

ex.en: I found them lying on the artificial grass.
ex.ja: 彼らは人工芝の上に横たわっていた。

ex.en: China is working on developing strong artificial intelligence.
ex.ja: 中国は強い人工知能の研究を進めている。

note.ja: ラテン語 artificialis ＝ ars（技）+ facere（作る）。「技で作られた」→「人工の」。art と同じ。

en: Below or underneath.
Below.
In a position that is lower in rank, dignity, etc.

beneath.ety: From Middle English benethe, from Old English bineoþan (“beneath, under, below”), equivalent to be- + neath. Cognate with Low German benedden (“beneath”), Dutch beneden (“beneath, under, down”), obsolete German benieden (“below”).

ex.en: The ice will crack beneath our weight.
ex.ja: 我々の重みで氷が割れるだろう。

ex.en: It is beneath him to say such a thing.
ex.ja: そんなことを言うとは彼らしくもない。

ex.en: It is beneath him to do something like that.
ex.ja: そのようなことをするのは彼の品位を落とす。

note.ja: be（〜に）+ neath（下に）。古英語 beneothan。「〜の下に」。underneath と同じ。

en: A projectile, usually of metal, shot from a gun at high speed.
An entire round of unfired ammunition for a firearm, including the projectile, the cartridge casing, the propellant charge, etc.
To draw attention to (text) by, or as if by, placing a graphic bullet in front of it.
To speed, like a bullet.

bullet.ety: From Middle English bullet (“an official tag or badge of registration or identification”), from Old French bullete, diminutive of boule (“ball”). Later influenced by Middle French boulette and French boulet.

ex.en: The bullet went right through his head.
ex.ja: 弾丸は彼の頭を貫通した。

ex.en: He was killed by a single bullet.
ex.ja: 彼は一発の弾丸で殺された。

ex.en: This gun is out of bullets.
ex.ja: この銃には弾が入っていません。

note.ja: フランス語 boulette（小さな球）から。boule（球）の指小辞。「弾丸」→ 箇条書きの「黒丸」。ball、bowl（球）と同系。※ bull（雄牛）とは別語源。

en: In a consistent manner.
constantly; always.

consistently.ety:
Etymology tree
English consistent
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English consistently
From consistent + -ly.

ex.en: He has consistently endeavored to help the poor.
ex.ja: 彼は一貫して貧しい人たちを助ける努力をしてきた。

note.ja: consistent（一貫した）+ -ly。con + sistere（立つ）。「共にしっかり立つ」→「一貫して」。consist と同じ。

en: The act of converting something or someone.
A software product converted from one platform to another.

conversion.ety: From Middle English conversion, conversioun, borrowed from Anglo-Norman conversion, from Latin conversiō, from convertō.

ex.en: The conversion of the old factory into apartments took two years.
ex.ja: 古い工場をアパートに改装するのに２年かかった。

note.ja: con（すっかり）+ vers（向ける）+ ion。向きをすっかり変えること →「転換・改宗・変換」。convert（変える）。

en: The right by law to be the entity which determines who may publish, copy and distribute a piece of writing, music, picture or other work …
Such an exclusive right as it pertains to one or more specific works.
To obtain or secure a copyright for some literary or other artistic work.

ex.en: Institutionally, a major restraint is the copyright problem.
ex.ja: 制度的に大きな枷となるのは、著作権の問題である。

note.ja: copy（写し）+ right（権利）。「複製する権利」→「著作権」。

en: Sediment or rock that is not native to its present location or is different from the surrounding material. Sometimes refers to ore or gems.
Bailment of personal property to be kept gratuitously for the bailor (depositor) and without any benefit to the bailee (depositary), e.g.…
To lay down; to place; to put.
To lay up or away for safekeeping; to put up; to store.

ex.en: Please deposit the money in a bank.
ex.ja: 銀行にそのお金を預けてください。

en: The place set for the end of a journey or to which something is sent; place or point aimed at.
Purpose for which anything is destined; predetermined end, object, or use; ultimate design.

destination.ety: From Latin dēstinātiō, from dēstinō (“to destine”).

ex.en: I reached my destination in a week.
ex.ja: 私は１週間で目的地についた。

ex.en: The ship reached its destination in safety.
ex.ja: 船は無事に目的地に着いた。

ex.en: After eating lunch, they headed for their next destination.
ex.ja: 昼食後、彼らは次の目的地に向かった。

note.ja: destine（運命づける）+ -ation。ラテン語 destinare（固定する・定める）。「定められた行き先」→「目的地」。destiny と同じ。

en: Soil or earth.
A stain or spot (on clothes etc); any foreign substance that worsens appearance.

dirt.ety:
From Middle English drit (“excrement”), from Old Norse drit (“excrement”), from Proto-Germanic *dritą, *dritō (“excrement”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰreyd-, *treydʰ- (“to have diarrhea”). Cognate with dialectal Danish and Norn drit (“excrement”), Norwegian dritt (“excrement”), dialectal Swedish dret (“shit”), Faroese and Icelandic drit (“bird excrement”), Dutch drijten (“to defecate”), drits (“dirt, mud, filth”), drijt and dreet (“excrement”), Low German drieten (“to defecate”), Driet (“shit”), regional German Driss (“shit”), Old English ġedrītan (“to defecate”).
The word originally referre

ex.en: The children were playing in the dirt.
ex.ja: 子供たちは泥んこの中で遊んでいた。

ex.en: Do you like playing in the dirt?
ex.ja: 土いじりは好きかい？

ex.en: When Mary was a child, her family was dirt poor.
ex.ja: メアリーが子供の頃、彼女の家はとても貧乏だった。

note.ja: 古北欧語 drit（糞）から。「汚れ」→「泥・土」。dirty。

zh: 多種多樣的 /多种多样的

en: Consisting of different elements; various.
Capable of or having various forms in different situations or at different times; multiform.
To make (something) different or varied in form or quality; to alter, to change, to vary.
To make the scope of (business, investments, etc.) different or varied, especially so as to balance and mitigate risks.

diverse.ety:
PIE word
 *dwóh₁
The adjective is derived from Middle English divers, diverse (“different, divergent”), from Anglo-Norman divers, Anglo-Norman divers, and Old French divers (“different; of various kinds”) (modern French divers), and directly from their etymon Latin dīversus (“different, diverse”), an adjective use of the perfect passive participle of dīvertō (“to divert, turn away”), from dī- (variant of dis- (prefix meaning ‘apart, in two’)) + vertō (“to turn”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *wert- (“to rotate; to turn”)). Doublet of divert.
The adverb is derived from Middle English div

ex.en: The vigorous man is engaged in diverse activities.
ex.ja: その精力的な男は様々な活動に加わっている。

ex.en: We find diverse ethnic and economic interests here.
ex.ja: ここでは多様な民族的・経済的利害関係がみられる。

note.ja: di（離れて）+ vers（向ける）+ e。別々の方向を向いた →「多様な」。

en: Of or pertaining to a god.
Eternal, holy, or otherwise godlike.
One skilled in divinity; a theologian.
A minister of the gospel; a priest; a clergyman.
To foretell (something), especially by the use of divination.
To guess or discover (something) through intuition or insight.

divine.ety: From Old French divin, from Latin dīvīnus (“of a god”), from divus (“god”). Displaced native Old English godcund.

ex.en: He worked under divine guidance.
ex.ja: 彼は神の導きのもとで働いた。

ex.en: To err is human, to forgive divine.
ex.ja: 間違いをするのが人間で、許すのは神だ。

ex.en: The cake tastes divine!
ex.ja: このケーキはすてき！

note.ja: ラテン語 divinus（神の）から。divus（神）。「神の・神聖な」→（口語）「すばらしい」。「占う」の divine も同じ語。

en: To the exclusion of anything or anyone else; solely or entirely.

exclusively.ety: From Middle English exclusyvely; equivalent to exclusive + -ly.

ex.en: I read detective stories exclusively.
ex.ja: 私は、もっぱら推理小説を読む。

ex.en: The privilege is reserved exclusively for women.
ex.ja: その特権はもっぱらご婦人だけに限られている。

note.ja: exclusive（独占的な）+ -ly。ex（外へ）+ claudere（閉じる）。「締め出して」→「もっぱら」。close と同系。

en: Of or relating to exportation or exports.
Something that is exported.
The act of exporting.
To carry away.
To sell (goods) to a foreign country.

ex.en: The firm has made large profits from exports.
ex.ja: その会社は輸出によって多額の利益を得た。

ex.en: Export of the product will start soon.
ex.ja: その製品の輸出はすぐ始まるだろう。

ex.en: Japanese industries export various products to America.
ex.ja: 日本の産業は種々の製品をアメリカに輸出している。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ port（運ぶ）。外へ運ぶ →「輸出（する）」。import（中へ運ぶ→輸入）と対。

en: At some time in the past.
Previously; once.

formerly.ety:
Etymology tree
English former
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English formerly
From former + -ly.

ex.en: Formerly this building was a hospital.
ex.ja: 昔はこの建物は病院だった。

ex.en: Formerly, this city was beautiful.
ex.ja: この町は昔きれいでした。

ex.en: Formerly, a book was worth its weight in silver, if not in gold.
ex.ja: 昔は、書物の価値は同じ重さの金とまでは行かないにしても、銀ぐらいの価値があった。

note.ja: former（前の）+ -ly。「以前は」。

en: In good working order.
Useful; serving a purpose, fulfilling a function.
A function that takes a function as its argument; more precisely, a function whose argument varies in a space of (real- or complex-valued…
A scalar-valued linear function on a vector space.

en: A father of someone's parent.
A male forefather.
To be, or act as, a grandfather to.

grandfather.ety: The noun is derived from Middle English grandfadre, graundfadir, graunfadir, grauntfader, and other forms, from graunt (“big, large; great, important”) + fā̆der (“male parent, father; remoter male ancestor”), probably modelled after Middle French grandpere, grant pere (“male parent; remoter male ancestor”) (whence French grand-père); the English word is analysable as grand- + father. Superseded earlier eldfather, elderfather. The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: Bob met her grandfather early in the morning.
ex.ja: ボブは朝早く彼女のおじいさんに会った。

ex.en: My grandfather is a bit hard of hearing.
ex.ja: おじいさんは少し耳が遠いんだ。

ex.en: My grandfather hopes that I will enter college.
ex.ja: 私のおじいちゃんは私が大学に行くことを望んでいる。

note.ja: grand（大きい・一世代上の）+ father。フランス語 grand-père の影響。

en: An action performed on a regular basis.
An action performed repeatedly and automatically, usually without awareness.
To clothe.
