ex.en: You must get rid of that bad habit.
ex.ja: 君はその悪い癖をなくさなければならない。

ex.en: You must get rid of such a habit.
ex.ja: そういうくせは直さなくてはならない。

ex.en: I have a habit of getting up early.
ex.ja: 私は朝早く起きる習慣がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 habere（持つ）から。hab + it。身に持っているもの →「習慣・癖」。inhabit（中に持つ→住む）も同じ。

en: To set apart or cut off from others.
To place in quarantine or isolation.
Something that has been isolated.
isolated.

isolate.ety: Back-formation from isolated, from French isolé, from Italian isolato, from Latin īnsulātus (whence also insulate), see -ate (etymology 1, 2 and 3).

ex.en: The village was isolated by the heavy storm.
ex.ja: その村はひどい嵐によって孤立した。

ex.en: We have isolated one patient from the rest.
ex.ja: 私たちは、一人の患者を残りの患者から隔離した。

ex.en: No nation can exist completely isolated from others.
ex.ja: 他の国から完全に独立して存在できる国などない。

note.ja: イタリア語 isolato（島にされた）から。isola（島）、ラテン語 insula。「孤立させる」。insulate、isle と同じ。

en: Suspecting rivalry in love; troubled by worries that one might have been replaced in someone's affections; suspicious of a lover's or spo…
Protective; zealously guarding; careful in the protection of something (or someone) one has or appreciates, especially one's spouse or lo…
To deliberately make (someone) jealous of another person's (often their partner's) associations with other people.

jealous.ety: First attested in 1382. From Middle English jelous, gelous, gelus, from Old French jalous, from Late Latin zelosus, from Ancient Greek ζῆλος (zêlos, “zeal, jealousy”). Doublet of zealous.

ex.en: I'm jealous that you have a good boss.
ex.ja: いい上司で羨ましいですね。

ex.en: You must not be jealous of others' success.
ex.ja: 他人の成功をねたんではならない。

ex.en: I'm jealous because you have a good boss.
ex.ja: いい上司で羨ましいですね。

note.ja: 古フランス語 gelos から。ラテン語 zelus（熱意）。zeal（熱意）と同じ語源。「熱心すぎる」→「嫉妬深い」。

en: Unwilling to do work or make an effort; disinclined to exertion.
Causing or characterised by idleness; relaxed or leisurely.
To laze, act in a lazy manner.
A lazy person.

lazy.ety:
Attested since 1540, origin uncertain. Probably from Low German and Middle Low German lasich (“slack, feeble, lazy”), from las, from Old Saxon lask, from Proto-Germanic *lasiwaz, *laskaz (“feeble, weak”), from Proto-Indo-European *las- (“weak”).
Akin to Dutch leuzig (“lazy”), German lässig (“casual, nonchalant, laid-back, easy-going”), Old Norse lasinn (“limpy, tired, weak”), Old English lesu, lysu (“false, evil, base”). More at lush.
An alternative etymology traces lazy to Early Modern English laysy, a derivative of lay (plural lays + -y) in the same way that tipsy is derived from tip. See la

ex.en: Stop being lazy and find something to do.
ex.ja: 家でごろごろするのをやめて、何かすることを見つけなさい。

ex.en: In the first place, he's a lazy boy.
ex.ja: まず第一に、彼は怠け者だ。

ex.en: John had been lazy before he met you.
ex.ja: ジョンはあなたに出会う前は怠け者でした。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。低地ドイツ語 lasich（だるい）とされる。

en: Synonym of mother (“a female parent”).
Synonym of mother (“an origin, a source”).
Often preceded by oh: used to express approval, joy, surprise, etc.
Synonym of mother (“to treat (someone) as a mother would be expected to treat her child; to nurture”).
To call out "mama".

mama.ety: The origin of the noun is uncertain; it is probably a reduplication of ma, thought to be a sound made by babies when breastfeeding. The word is possibly influenced by Middle French maman (“mother”) (modern French maman), mamme (both probably from Latin mamma (“breast; nurse; (childish) mother, mama; grandmother”), probably cognate with Ancient Greek μᾰ́μμη (mắmmē, “breast; (childish) mother, mama; (Koine) grandmother”), both possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂- (“to nurse; mama, mother”)), but this is also uncertain as all the words could have developed independently as onomatop

ex.en: Mama, is it okay if I go swimming?
ex.ja: お母さん、泳ぎに行ってもいい？

ex.en: Mama seems to have started with French.
ex.ja: お母さんがフランス語始めたっぽい。

ex.en: I still call my mother Mama.
ex.ja: お母さんのこと、まだママって呼んでるよ。

note.ja: 幼児語。世界の多くの言語に似た形がある。

en: To change part of.
To be or become modified.

modify.ety: From Middle English modifien, from Middle French modifier, from Latin modificare (“to limit, control, regulate, deponent”), from modificari (“to measure off, set bound to, moderate”), from modus (“measure”) + facere (“to make”); see mode.

ex.en: We want to modify the regulations of our school.
ex.ja: 私達は校則を修正したい。

ex.en: We usually modify our views in college.
ex.ja: 普通、私達は大学で自分の考えを修正します。

ex.en: To suit the English language, the translation was modified.
ex.ja: 英語にあわせ、訳を変更しました。

note.ja: ラテン語 modificare ＝ modus（尺度）+ facere。「尺度に合わせる」→「修正する・修飾する」。mode と同じ。

en: Of or pertaining to a municipality (a city or a corporation having the right of administering local government).
Of or pertaining to the internal affairs of a nation.
A financial instrument issued by a municipality (e.g., municipal bonds).

municipal.ety: Borrowed from French municipal, from Latin mūnicipālis (“of or belonging to a citizen or a free town”), from mūniceps (“a citizen, an inhabitant of a free town”), from mūnus (“duty”) + capiō (“to take”).

ex.en: The municipal council should concentrate more on specific issues.
ex.ja: 市議会は具体的な問題にもっと焦点をあてるべきだ。

ex.en: The municipal council all but ignored the gravity of the pollution.
ex.ja: 市議会はその汚染の重大さをほとんど無視した。

ex.en: The municipal government is at their wits' end concerning the garbage problem.
ex.ja: 自治体はゴミ処理問題に頭を抱えている。

note.ja: mun（務め）+ i + cip（取る）+ al。務めを引き受ける自治都市の →「市の・地方自治の」。

en: Of or relating to a navy.
Of or relating to ships in general.

naval.ety: From Middle English naval, from Middle French naval, from Latin nāvālis; equivalent to navy + -al.

ex.en: He has received a commission as a naval officer.
ex.ja: 彼は海軍士官の任務を受けた。

note.ja: ラテン語 navalis（船の）から。navis（船）。「海軍の」。navy と同じ。navel（へそ）とは別語。

ex.en: The neighbors took turns sitting up with him.
ex.ja: 近所の人々が彼とともに、交替で夜を明かした。

ex.en: The French are our neighbors across the Channel.
ex.ja: フランス人はイギリス海峡を越えた私たちの隣人だ。

ex.en: Sister cities are the same as good neighbors.
ex.ja: 姉妹都市はよき隣人と同じである。

note.ja: 古英語 nēahgebūr ＝ nēah（近い）+ gebūr（住人）。「近くに住む人」。near、boor と同系。

en: Not taking sides in a conflict such as war; nonaligned.
Favoring neither the supporting nor opposing viewpoint of a topic of debate; unbiased.
A nonaligned state, or a member of such a state.
A person who takes no side in a dispute.

neutral.ety: From Middle French neutral (compare modern French neutre), from Latin neutrālis. By surface analysis, neuter + -al.

ex.en: That country remained neutral throughout World War II.
ex.ja: その国は第二次世界大戦中は中立を保っていた。

ex.en: The Japanese government takes a neutral attitude on the matter.
ex.ja: 日本政府はその件に関しては中立の態度をとっている。

ex.en: He was a neutral participant at the discussion.
ex.ja: 彼は話し合いでは中立の立場をとった。

note.ja: ラテン語 neutralis から。neuter（どちらでもない）＝ ne + uter（どちらか）。「中立の・中性の」。

en: An aristocrat; one of aristocratic blood.
A medieval gold coin of England in the 14th and 15th centuries, usually valued at 6s 8d.
Having honorable qualities; having moral eminence and freedom from anything petty, mean or dubious in conduct and character.
Grand; stately; magnificent; splendid.

noble.ety:
From Middle English noble, from Old French noble, borrowed from Latin nōbilis (“knowable, known, well-known, famous, celebrated, high-born, of noble birth, excellent”), from nōscere, gnōscere (“to know”).
False cognate of Arabic نبيل (nabīl). Displaced native English athel, from Old English æþele.

ex.en: I am certain that you have noble thoughts.
ex.ja: 私はあなたが気高い心の持ち主だと確信している。

ex.en: He is a man of noble blood.
ex.ja: 彼は高貴な家柄の人です。

ex.en: He is a man of noble birth.
ex.ja: 彼は高貴な生まれの人です。

note.ja: ラテン語 nobilis（知られた・高貴な）から。noscere（知る）。「名の知られた」→「貴族の・高潔な」。know、notable と同じ祖先。

en: The sound of a light slap or tap with a soft flat object, especially of a footstep.
A light tap or slap, especially with the hands.
To (gently) tap the flat of one's hand on a person or thing.
To hit lightly and repeatedly with the flat of the hand to make smooth or flat
Exactly suitable, fitting, apt; timely, convenient, opportune, ready for the occasion; especially of things spoken.
Trite, being superficially complete, lacking originality.
Opportunely, in a timely or suitable way.
Perfectly.

pat.ety: From Middle English pat (“a blow, stroke”), alteration (with loss of medial l) of *plat (> Scots plat (“a blow, buffet”)), from Old English plætt (“a sounding blow, a smack”), from Proto-West Germanic *platt (“a smack, slap, blow”), from Proto-Germanic *plat- (“to strike, beat”), from Proto-Indo-European *blod-, *bled- (“to strike, beat”). Cognate with Middle Dutch plat (“a smack, blow, slap”), Middle Low German plat (“a smack, blow, beating”), Middle High German plaz, blaz (“a resounding blow, bang, crash”). For loss of l, compare patch for platch; pate for plate, etc. See plat.

ex.en: I saw him pat her on the shoulder.
ex.ja: 私は彼が彼女の肩をたたくのを見た。

ex.en: I felt somebody pat me on the shoulder.
ex.ja: 誰かが私の肩をたたいたのを感じた。

ex.en: I felt somebody patting on my shoulder from behind.
ex.ja: 私はだれかが背後から肩をたたいているのを感じた。

note.ja: 擬音的な語。「軽くたたく」→ pat on the back（ほめる）。

en: The quality or state of being popular; especially, the state of being widely liked or in favor with the people at large.
Something that is popular.

popularity.ety: From popular + -ity, from Latin popularitas (“an effort to please the people”).

ex.en: The actor died at the height of his popularity.
ex.ja: その俳優は人気絶頂の時に死んだ。

ex.en: The popularity of a web site depends on its content.
ex.ja: ホームページの人気は内容次第。

ex.en: The magazine is enjoying great popularity.
ex.ja: その雑誌は大変人気がある。

note.ja: popular（人気のある）+ -ity。ラテン語 populus（民衆）。「民衆に好まれること」。people と同じ。

en: A system of serfdom used in Central Europe, under which a tenant's rent was paid in forced labour.

robot.ety: From German Robot, from a West Slavic language, ultimately related to Etymology 2, below.

ex.en: That computer is what we call a robot.
ex.ja: そのコンピューターはいわゆるロボットである。

ex.en: He is, so to speak, a human robot.
ex.ja: 彼はいわばロボット人間だ。

ex.en: It only shows you're not a robot.
ex.ja: 君がロボットではないってことは分かる。

note.ja: チェコの作家チャペックが戯曲（1920年）で作った語。チェコ語 robota（強制労働）。

en: Characterized by solemn religious ceremony or religious use, especially, in a positive sense; consecrated, made holy.
Religious; relating to religion, or to the services of religion; not secular

sacred.ety: From Middle English sacred, isacred, past participle of sacren, sakeren (“to make holy, hallow”), equivalent to sacre + -ed.

ex.en: Cows are sacred to many people in India.
ex.ja: インドに暮らす多くの人にとって牛は神聖である。

ex.en: In India, the cow is a sacred animal.
ex.ja: インドでは牛は神聖な動物です。

ex.en: Church is a sacred place.
ex.ja: 教会は神聖な場です。

note.ja: ラテン語 sacrare（神聖にする）の過去分詞から。sacer（神聖な）。sacrifice、sacrament と同じ。

en: A person who secretly watches and examines the actions of other individuals or organizations and gathers information on them (usually to …
A defensive player assigned to cover an offensive backfield player man-to-man when they are expected to engage in a running play, but the…
To act as a spy.
To spot; to catch sight of; to espy.

spy.ety:
From Middle English spien, aphetic variant of earlier espien (“to espy”), from Old French espier (“to spy”), from Frankish *spehōn (“to spy”), from Proto-Germanic *spehōną (“to see, look”), from Proto-Indo-European *speḱ- (“to look”). Akin to German spähen (“to spy”), Dutch spieden (“to spy”).
The noun displaced native Old English sċēawere (literally “watcher”), which was also the word for "mirror." In this sense, the verb displaced Old English sċēawian, which was also the word for "to watch" and became the Modern English word show.
Distant cognate vie PIE with Latin speculātor, Ancient Greek

ex.ja: 詳しく調べると彼がスパイであることがわかった。

ex.en: Do you really think Tom is a spy?
ex.ja: 本当にトムがスパイだと思ってるの？

ex.en: The spy has made contact with the enemy.
ex.ja: スパイは敵と接触した。

note.ja: 古フランス語 espier（見張る）から。espionage（スパイ活動）と同じ。

en: Something suggested (with subsequent adposition being for)
The act of suggesting.

suggestion.ety: From Middle English suggestion, from Anglo-Norman suggestioun, sugestiun, from Latin suggestiō, from suggerō (“suggest”, verb), from Latin sub- (“from below, up”) + gerō (“to bring”). Equivalent to suggest + -ion. Related to English up-, cast.

ex.en: Your suggestion will be rejected by the teacher.
ex.ja: 君の提案は先生に拒否されるだろう。

ex.en: The new hotel invited suggestions from the guests.
ex.ja: その新しいホテルではお客さんに意見を求めた。

ex.en: Our suggestions were, in effect, almost the same.
ex.ja: 私たちの提案は実質にほとんど同じだった。

note.ja: sug（下から）+ gest（運ぶ）+ ion。下からそっと持ち出すこと →「提案・示唆」。

en: The act of suspending, or the state of being suspended.
A temporary or conditional delay, interruption or discontinuation.

suspension.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin suspensiōnem (“arching, vaulting; suspension”), from suspendēre (“to hang up, to suspend”), from sub- (“under”) + pendere (“to hang, to suspend”), from Proto-Italic *pendō (“to hang, to put in a hanging position”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pénd-e-ti, from *(s)pend- (“to pull; to spin”)). Compare Anglo-Norman suspensiun, French suspension, Occitan suspensio.

ex.en: There is a suspension bridge ahead of us.
ex.ja: 私たちの目の前に吊り橋がある。

ex.en: The suspension bridge is 5 miles upstream.
ex.ja: つり橋は５マイル上流にある。

ex.ja: 現在のバージョンは、アップグレード版で置き換えます。

en: Authorization or certification; a sanction, as given by a superior.
Something that provides assurance or confirmation; a guarantee or proof.
To guarantee (something) to be (of a specified quality, value, etc.).
To guarantee as being true; (colloquial) to believe strongly.

warrant.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English warant (“protector; guard, shield, protection”), from Anglo-Norman warrant, Old Northern French warant, warand, a variant of Old French guarant, garant, garand (“assurance, guarantee; authorization, permission; protector; protection, safety”) (modern French garant), from Frankish *warand, present participle of *warjan (“to fend off; to stop, thwart”). The word is cognate with Old High German werento (“guarantor”).
The verb is derived from Middle English warrant, waranten (“to give protection; to protect, shield; to assure, pledge, promise; to guarantee”)

ex.ja: 私たちは彼の行動は正しかったということに同意した。

ex.ja: 捜索令状は持っているのですか。

ex.ja: ベーカーさん一家は河の上流に農場を持っている。

ex.en: I am blessed if I know it.
ex.ja: そんなこと知るもんか。

note.ja: 古英語 blētsian（血で清める）から。blood と同系とされる。「祝福する」。

A responsibility, onus.
To encumber with a burden.
To impose, as a load or burden; to lay or place as a burden (something heavy or objectionable).

ex.ja: 彼は家計の上で彼女の負担にはなっていなかった。

ex.en: I'm afraid I'll be a burden to you.
ex.ja: 僕は君に厄介になるんじゃないかな。

ex.ja: 広島と長崎で亡くなった罪のない市民の数はどれくらいですか？

To train someone by instruction and practice.
To teach someone to obey authority.

discipline.ety: From Middle English [Term?], from Anglo-Norman, from Old French descipline, from Latin disciplina (“instruction”), from discipulus (“pupil”), influenced by disco (“to learn”), from Proto-Indo-European *dek- (“(cause to) accept”).

ex.en: School discipline is not as it should be.
ex.ja: 学校の規律が乱れている。

ex.en: One's talent is in need of discipline.
ex.ja: 才能は訓練を必要とする。

ex.en: Learning poetry is a good discipline for the memory.
ex.ja: 詩を習うことは記憶力を養うよい訓練となる。

note.ja: ラテン語 disciplina（教え）から。discipulus（弟子）。「教え」→「規律・しつけ」→「学問分野」。disciple と同じ。

en: Causing disgust; repulsive; distasteful.

ex.en: The very idea of it is disgusting.
ex.ja: それを思うだけでも気持ちが悪い。

ex.en: That attitude of his is quite disgusting.
ex.ja: 彼のあの態度、感じ悪いわね。

ex.en: Why are you eating this disgusting stuff?
ex.ja: なんでこんなまずいもの食ってんの？

note.ja: disgust（嫌悪）+ -ing。dis（否定）+ gustus（味）。「味がまずい」→「むかつく」。gusto と同じ。

en: The fifth major tone of a musical scale (five major steps above the note in question); thus G is the dominant of C, A of D, and so on.
The triad built on the dominant tone.
Ruling; governing; prevailing
Predominant, common, prevalent, of greatest importance.

ex.en: Efficiency is the dominant idea in business.
ex.ja: 商売では能率のよさということが最も重要な考えである。

ex.en: The human race is dominant on earth.
ex.ja: 人類は地球上で最も優勢である。

ex.en: Opinion against the direct tax was dominant.
ex.ja: 直接税に反対する意見が支配的だった。

note.ja: ラテン語 dominari（支配する）から。dominus（主人）。「支配的な」。dominate、domain と同じ dom。

en: A written composition of moderate length, exploring a particular issue or subject.
A proposed design for a postage stamp or a banknote.
To move forth, as into battle.

essay.ety: Since late 16th century, borrowed from Middle French essay, essai (“essay”), meaning coined by Montaigne at the same time, from the same words with the earlier meanings 'experiment; assay; attempt', from Old French essay, essai, assay, assai, from Latin exagium (“weight; weighing, testing on the balance”), from exigere + -ium.

ex.en: All essays must be handed in on time.
ex.ja: すべてのレポートは期限を守って提出されなければならない。

ex.en: I've got to finish this essay by tomorrow.
ex.ja: 私はあしたまでにこの作文を書き上げなければならない。

ex.en: Who wrote this essay? It has no name.
ex.ja: この作文を書いた人は誰ですか。名前がありません。

note.ja: 古フランス語 essai（試み）から。ラテン語 exagium（量ること）。モンテーニュの『エセー（試み）』から「随筆」。

en: In addition; besides; further; what's more (i.e. to denote additional information).

furthermore.ety: From Middle English furthermore, forthermore, forthermar (also as forther mo), equivalent to further + -more.

ex.en: The hotel is cheap; furthermore, it is close to the station.
ex.ja: そのホテルは安いうえに、駅にも近い。

note.ja: further（さらに）+ more。「さらに」。

en: Drawn, pictorial.
Explicit, vivid, descriptive, often in relation to depictions of sex or violence.
A drawing or picture.
A computer-generated image as viewed on a screen forming part of a game or a film etc.

graphic.ety: From Latin graphicus (“belonging to painting or drawing”), from Ancient Greek γραφικός (graphikós, “belonging to painting or drawing, picturesque, of or for writing; of style, lively”), from γραφή (graphḗ, “drawing, painting, writing, a writing, description, etc.”), from γράφω (gráphō, “scratch, carve”) (cognate with English carve).

ex.en: She works as a graphic designer.
ex.ja: 彼女はグラフィックデザイナーとして働いている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 graphein（書く・描く）から。graph + ic。描かれた →「図の・生々しい・画像」。

en: The process where the cells in the body regenerate and repair themselves.
An act of healing, as by a faith healer.

healing.ety: From Middle English heelinge, helynge, from Old English hǣling (“healing”), from Proto-Germanic *hailingō (“healing”), from Proto-Germanic *hailijaną (“to heal”), equivalent to heal + -ing. Cognate with West Frisian hieling (“healing”), Dutch heling (“healing”), German Heilung (“healing; cure”).

ex.en: Healing the wounds of the heart takes time.
ex.ja: 心の傷を癒すには時間がかかる。

ex.en: These hot springs possess properties for healing wounds.
ex.ja: この温泉は傷を治す性質がある。

note.ja: heal（治す）+ -ing。heal は whole（完全な）と同じ語根で「完全にする」。

en: To bring about; to put into practice; to carry out.
To realize a technical specification, e.g. of an algorithm, interface, or protocol.
A tool or instrument for working with.

implement.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin implēmentum (“a filling up”), from Latin impleō (“to fill up”).

ex.en: These implements are in common use.
ex.ja: これらの道具は一般に用いられている。

ex.en: The merger was implemented on a 50-50 ratio.
ex.ja: その合併は１対１で行われた。

ex.en: They implemented a communication policy so as to promote their new concept.
ex.ja: 彼らは自分たちの新しいコンセプトを広めるためにあるコミュニケーションポリシーを採用した。

note.ja: ラテン語 implere（満たす）から。「満たすもの」→「道具」→「実行する」。complete と同じ ple。

As soon as, directly.

en: A military action consisting of a large armed force of one geopolitical entity entering territory controlled by another such entity, gene…
The entry without consent of an individual or group into an area where they are not wanted.

invasion.ety: From Middle French invasion, from Late Latin invāsiōnem, accusative of invāsiō.

ex.en: It is nothing less than an invasion.
ex.ja: それはまさに侵略行為だ。

ex.en: It's a fort built to defend the town from invasion.
ex.ja: それは侵略から街を守るために造られた要塞だ。

ex.en: This is an invasion of privacy!
ex.ja: こんなのプライバシーの侵害だ。

note.ja: invade（侵略する）+ -sion。in + vadere（行く）。「中へ入っていく」→「侵略」。evade と同じ vad。

en: A laptop computer.
Designed for use on a lap.
To use a laptop computer.

laptop.ety: From lap (“upper legs of a seated person”) + top, modeled after desktop.

ex.en: Can I use my laptop in the bath?
ex.ja: お風呂でパソコンって、使えますか？

ex.en: "Where is my laptop?" "It's on the chair."
ex.ja: 「私のパソコンどこ？」「椅子の上にあるよ」

ex.en: Tom closed his laptop and stood up.
ex.ja: トムはノートパソコンを閉じ、立ち上がった。

note.ja: lap（ひざ）+ top（上）。「ひざの上に置くもの」→「ノートパソコン」。desktop の対。

en: Of or pertaining to a legend or to legends.
Appearing (solely) in legends.
A legendary Pokémon.

legendary.ety: From legend + -ary; from Medieval Latin legendārius. Earlier it was a noun meaning "a collection of legends" (1510s) (Medieval Latin legendārium, Old French legendier), from Latin legenda. In English, both the noun and the adjective first appeared in the 16th century.

ex.en: Bill is still a legendary figure in this company.
ex.ja: ビルはこの会社での語り草になっている。

note.ja: legend（伝説）+ -ary。ラテン語 legenda（読まれるべきもの）、legere（読む）。聖人伝 →「伝説」。

God, the Creator.

ex.ja: 真の歴史を形成するのは大衆である。

ex.ja: 銃器メーカーは小火器による暴力事件に対する責任を逃れてきた。

ex.en: I want to become a bisque doll maker.
ex.ja: 私は将来ビスクドール作家になりたい。

note.ja: make（作る）+ -er。「作る人・製造業者」。

en: One who opposes another; one who works or takes a position against someone or something; one who attempts to stop the progress of someone…
One who opposes another physically (in a fight, sport, game, or competition).

opponent.ety: Borrowed from Latin oppōnēns (“opposing”), present active participle of oppōnō (“to oppose”).

ex.en: The team had advantage over their opponents.
ex.ja: そのチームは相手よりまさっていた。

ex.en: He got the better of his opponent.
ex.ja: 彼は相手を打ち負かした。

ex.en: Off-target. My opponent hadn't been hit.
ex.ja: 外れた。相手に着弾していない。

note.ja: ラテン語 opponere ＝ ob（反対に）+ ponere（置く）。「反対側に置かれた人」→「対戦相手」。oppose と同じ pon。

Pertaining to charity administered or received away from, or independently from, a workhouse or other institution.
To publicly display a child after it has been named

note.ja: out（外の）+ door（戸）。「戸外の」。

en: Any of various evergreen trees from the family Palmae or Arecaceae, which are mainly found in the tropics.
A branch or leaf of the palm, anciently borne or worn as a symbol of victory or rejoicing.
To hold or conceal something in the palm of the hand, e.g., for an act of sleight of hand or to steal something.
To hold something without bending the fingers significantly.

palm.ety: From Middle English palme, from Old English palm, palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch”), from Latin palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch, palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₂meh₂, *pl̥h₂emeh₂ (“palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”). Cognate with Dutch palm, German Palme, Danish palme, Icelandic pálmur (“palm”).

ex.en: All right then, show me your palms.
ex.ja: では、手のひらを見せてください。

ex.en: I am interested in palm reading.
ex.ja: 手相に興味があるんです。

ex.en: I'm interested in palm reading.
ex.ja: 手相に興味があるんです。

note.ja: ラテン語 palma（手のひら）から。ヤシの葉が広げた手のひらに似ていることから「ヤシ」も表す。

A construction by which an animal is harnessed to a carriage.
To propel by pushing with poles, to push with a pole.
To identify something quite precisely using a telescope.

en: The act of receiving.
The act or ability to receive radio or similar signals.

reception.ety: From Middle English recepcion, reception, from Middle French reception, from Latin receptiōn- (“the act of receiving; reception”), from recipiō (“receive”), from re- (“back”) + capiō (“to hold”). Equivalent to receive + -tion.

ex.en: There were beautiful flowers on the reception desk.
ex.ja: きれいな花が受付のデスクに飾ってありました。

ex.en: There was a big reception after the wedding.
ex.ja: 結婚式の後で盛大な披露宴が催された。

ex.en: Old friends were invited to the reception.
ex.ja: 旧友がレセプションに招かれた。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ cept（取る）+ ion。受け取ること →「受付・歓迎会・受信」。receive（受け取る）。

en: Any set of instructions for preparing a mixture of ingredients.
A plan or procedure to obtain a given end result; a prescription.

recipe.ety: Borrowed from Middle French récipé, from Latin recipe, second person singular imperative of Latin recipiō (“receive”).

ex.en: The recipe serves six people.
ex.ja: その作り方の分量は六人分です。

ex.en: This is my special recipe.
ex.ja: これは私のスペシャルレシピです。

ex.en: The recipe is easy.
ex.ja: 作り方は簡単よ。

note.ja: ラテン語 recipere（受け取る）の命令形「取れ」から。処方箋の冒頭の言葉 →「調理法・秘訣」。receive と同じ cap。

en: Of or pertaining to regulation.

ex.en: The drug is waiting for regulatory approval.
ex.ja: その薬は規制当局の承認を待っている。

note.ja: regulate（規制する）+ -ory。「規制の」。rule と同じ語源。
